title.zh: 卷一 本紀第一 武帝上
title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一 武帝上 Volume 1 Annals 1: Emperor Wu 1

sentences.zh: 初為冠軍孫無終司馬。

translations.literal: At first he served as marshal under Champion General Sun Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as marshal on the staff of Champion General Sun Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 安帝隆安三年十一月，妖賊孫恩作亂於會稽，晉朝衞將軍謝琰、前將軍劉牢之東討。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Long'an under Emperor An, the demonic rebel Sun En rose in revolt in Kuaiji; the Jin dynasty's Defender-in-Chief Xie Yan and Forward General Liu Laozhi marched east to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Long'an (399), while Emperor An still reigned, the rebel Sun En broke out in Kuaiji. The Jin court sent Defender-in-Chief Xie Yan and Forward General Liu Laozhi east against him.

sentences.zh: 牢之請高祖參府軍事。

translations.literal: Laozhi requested that Gaozu join his staff as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi asked Gaozu to serve on his headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 十二月，牢之至吳，而賊緣道屯結，牢之命高祖與數十人覘賊遠近。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, when Laozhi reached Wu, the bandits had entrenched themselves all along the route; Laozhi ordered Gaozu, with several dozen men, to reconnoiter how near or far the enemy were.
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month Laozhi reached Wu. The rebels had set up camps all along the roads, and he sent Gaozu out with a few dozen men to scout their positions.

sentences.zh: 會遇賊至，眾數千人，高祖便進與戰。

translations.literal: They happened to meet the bandits arriving—several thousand strong—and Gaozu at once advanced to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: They ran straight into the enemy: several thousand men. Gaozu charged to fight them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 所將人多死，而戰意方厲，手奮長刀，所殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Most of the men he led were killed, yet his fighting spirit only grew fiercer; wielding a long blade in his hand, he killed and wounded a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his party fell, but he fought all the harder, swinging a long saber and cutting down a great number of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 牢之子敬宣疑高祖淹久，恐為賊所困，乃輕騎尋之。

translations.literal: Laozhi's son Jingxuan, fearing that Gaozu had been away too long and might be trapped by the bandits, rode out lightly to search for him.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi's son Jingxuan worried that Gaozu had been gone too long and might be surrounded. He took a light escort and went to find him.

sentences.zh: 既而眾騎並至，賊乃奔退，斬獲千餘人，推鋒而進，平山陰，恩遁還入海。

translations.literal: Presently the main cavalry force also arrived; the bandits then broke and fled. More than a thousand were killed or captured. Pressing the attack, they pacified Shanyin, and En fled back out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rest of the cavalry came up. The rebels broke and ran. Over a thousand were killed or taken. The army pushed forward, pacified Shanyin, and En escaped back to sea.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，恩復入會稽，殺衞將軍謝琰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, En again entered Kuaiji and killed Defender-in-Chief Xie Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year (400), En invaded Kuaiji again and killed Xie Yan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，劉牢之復率眾東征，恩退走。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Liu Laozhi once more led his troops on an eastern campaign, and En retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Laozhi marched east again, and En withdrew.

sentences.zh: 牢之屯上虞，使高祖戍句章城。

translations.literal: Laozhi encamped at Shangyu and had Gaozu garrison Goukou.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi camped at Shangyu and left Gaozu to hold Goukou.

sentences.zh: 句章城既卑小，戰士不盈數百人，高祖常被堅執銳，為士卒先，每戰輒摧鋒陷陣，賊乃退還浹口。

translations.literal: Goukou was low and small, and the fighting men numbered no more than a few hundred; Gaozu often donned stout armor and sharp weapons, taking the lead among the soldiers; in every battle he would break the enemy front and storm their formations, and the bandits then withdrew to Jiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Goukou was a mean little fortress with only a few hundred defenders. Gaozu always armed himself heavily and led from the front. In every fight he smashed the enemy line, until the rebels fell back to Jiakou.

sentences.zh: 于時東伐諸帥，御軍無律，士卒暴掠，甚為百姓所苦。

translations.literal: At that time the commanders on the eastern campaign kept no discipline over their armies, and the soldiers plundered violently, to the great distress of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern commanders as a rule kept no discipline, and their troops looted the countryside until the people were desperate.

sentences.zh: 唯高祖法令明整，所至莫不親賴焉。

translations.literal: Only Gaozu's laws and orders were clear and strict; wherever he went, none failed to trust and rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Gaozu were regulations clear and troops orderly. Wherever he marched, people trusted him.

sentences.zh: 五年春，孫恩頻攻句章，高祖屢摧破之，恩復走入海。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, Sun En repeatedly attacked Goukou; Gaozu repeatedly shattered his forces, and En again fled out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year (401) Sun En attacked Goukou again and again. Gaozu beat him back each time, and En once more took to sea.

sentences.zh: 三月，恩北出海鹽，高祖追而翼之，築城于海鹽故治。

translations.literal: In the third month, En went north out of sea by way of Haiyan; Gaozu pursued and flanked him, building a fort at the old seat of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month En came north from the sea toward Haiyan. Gaozu pursued and outflanked him, building a walled camp at the old Haiyan seat.

sentences.zh: 賊日來攻城，城內兵力甚弱，高祖乃選敢死之士數百人，咸脫甲冑，執短兵，並鼓噪而出，賊震懼奪氣，因其懼而奔之，並棄甲散走，斬其大帥姚盛。

translations.literal: The bandits came daily to assault the city; the forces inside were very weak. Gaozu then selected several hundred daredevils, all stripped of armor, grasping short weapons; together they rushed out with war cries. The bandits were shaken and lost their nerve; taking advantage of their fear, he charged them. They all cast off armor and scattered in flight, and their great commander Yao Sheng was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked every day, and the garrison was desperately weak. Gaozu picked several hundred volunteers, stripped them of armor, armed them with short weapons, and sent them out yelling. The enemy panicked. He struck while they were still afraid; they threw down their armor and fled, and he killed their commander Yao Sheng.

sentences.zh: 雖連戰剋勝，然眾寡不敵，高祖獨深慮之。

translations.literal: Though he won victory in battle after battle, his numbers could not match the enemy, and Gaozu alone was deeply troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: He won fight after fight, yet he was badly outnumbered, and the situation weighed on him.

sentences.zh: 一夜，偃旗匿眾，若已遁者。

translations.literal: One night he lowered the banners and hid his troops, as if he had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: One night he furled the banners and hid his men, making it look as though he had abandoned the place.

sentences.zh: 明晨開門，使羸疾數人登城。

translations.literal: At dawn he opened the gates and had a few sick and weak men climb the wall.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he opened the gates and put a few sick or feeble men on the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 賊遙問劉裕所在。

translations.literal: From afar the bandits asked where Liu Yu was.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shouted from a distance, asking where Liu Yu was.

sentences.zh: 曰：「夜已走矣。

translations.literal: They replied: "He fled in the night.
translations.idiomatic: The men on the wall answered, "He got away last night.

sentences.zh: 」賊信之，乃率眾大上。

translations.literal: " The bandits believed it and then led their masses up in force.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy believed them and stormed the walls in strength.

sentences.zh: 高祖乘其懈怠，奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Gaozu, taking advantage of their slackness, struck fiercely and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu waited until they had grown careless, then hit them hard and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 恩知城不可下，乃進向滬瀆。

translations.literal: En, knowing the city could not be taken, then advanced toward Hudu.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city could not be taken, En marched on toward Hudu.

sentences.zh: 高祖復棄城追之。

translations.literal: Gaozu again abandoned the city to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu again left the fort and pursued him.

sentences.zh: 海鹽令鮑陋遣子嗣之以吳兵一千，請為前驅。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Haiyan, Bao Lou, sent his son Sizhi with a thousand Wu troops, asking to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Lou, magistrate of Haiyan, sent his son Sizhi with a thousand Wu soldiers and offered to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「賊兵甚精，吳人不習戰，若前驅失利，必敗我軍。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "The bandit soldiers are very skilled; the men of Wu are not accustomed to fighting. If the vanguard suffers defeat, it will surely ruin our army.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The rebels fight well, and Wu men are not used to war. If your van is broken, you will take our whole force with you.

sentences.zh: 可在後為聲援。

translations.literal: You should stay in the rear as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: Stay behind us and lend support from the rear.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " They did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: " They would not listen.

sentences.zh: 是夜，高祖多設伏兵，兼置旗鼓，然一處不過數人。

translations.literal: That night Gaozu set many ambushes and also planted flags and drums, yet at any one spot there were no more than a few men.
translations.idiomatic: That night he laid many ambushes and set out flags and drums, but at each point there were only a handful of men.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊率眾萬餘迎戰。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits led more than ten thousand men to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the enemy came out with more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 前驅既交，諸伏皆出，舉旗鳴鼓。

translations.literal: Once the vanguard had engaged, all the ambushes came forth, raising flags and beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: When the van clashed, every ambush party rose, raising banners and beating drums.

sentences.zh: 賊謂四面有軍，乃退。

translations.literal: The bandits thought armies were on all four sides and then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thought they were surrounded on every side and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 嗣之追奔，為賊所沒。

translations.literal: Sizhi pursued the fleeing enemy and was overwhelmed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi chased the retreat and was cut off and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 高祖且戰且退，賊盛，所領死傷且盡。

translations.literal: Gaozu fought as he withdrew; the bandits were strong, and those he led were killed and wounded until nearly all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu fought a fighting retreat. The enemy pressed hard, and nearly all his men were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 高祖慮不免，至向伏兵處，乃止，令左右脫取死人衣。

translations.literal: Gaozu feared he could not escape; when he reached the place of the ambush, he halted and ordered those beside him to strip the dead of their clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He thought he would not get away alive. When he reached the ambush ground he stopped and told his companions to strip clothing from the corpses.

sentences.zh: 賊謂當走反停，疑猶有伏。

translations.literal: The bandits thought that when one should flee he instead halted, and suspected there were still ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy expected a rout, yet he had halted; they suspected another trap.

sentences.zh: 高祖因呼更戰，氣色甚猛，賊眾以為然，乃引軍去。

translations.literal: Gaozu then shouted for another fight; his bearing was very fierce, and the bandit masses believed it and so led their army away.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu called for another charge, looking ferocious. The rebels took him at his word and drew off.

sentences.zh: 高祖徐歸，然後散兵稍集。

translations.literal: Gaozu withdrew slowly; only then did his scattered troops gradually reassemble.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew at an easy pace, and only then did his scattered men begin to gather again.

sentences.zh: 五月，孫恩破滬瀆，殺吳國內史袁山松，死者四千人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Sun En broke through at Hudu and killed Interior Minister of Wu Yuan Shansong; four thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Sun En overran Hudu and killed Yuan Shansong, interior minister of Wu; four thousand people died.

sentences.zh: 是月，高祖復破賊於婁縣。

translations.literal: That month Gaozu again defeated the bandits at Lou county.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Gaozu beat the rebels again at Lou.

sentences.zh: 六月，恩乘勝浮海，奄至丹徒，戰士十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, En, riding his victory, came by sea and suddenly reached Dantu, with a hundred thousand or more fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month En sailed in on the momentum of his victories and suddenly appeared at Dantu with more than a hundred thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之猶屯山陰，京邑震動。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi was still encamped at Shanyin, and the capital region was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi was still at Shanyin, and the capital was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 高祖倍道兼行，與賊俱至。

translations.literal: Gaozu pressed on by forced marches day and night and arrived with the bandits at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu forced the march day and night and reached the scene as the enemy did.

sentences.zh: 于時眾力既寡，加以步遠疲勞，而丹徒守軍莫有鬭志。

translations.literal: At that time their strength was already scant, and in addition the long march on foot had wearied them, while the garrison at Dantu had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: His force was small to begin with, and the long foot march had exhausted them. The Dantu garrison had no stomach for a fight.

sentences.zh: 恩率眾數萬，鼓噪登蒜山，居民皆荷擔而立。

translations.literal: En led tens of thousands of men, beating drums and shouting as they climbed Garlic Hill; the inhabitants all shouldered their packs and stood ready.
translations.idiomatic: En brought tens of thousands up Garlic Hill with drums and war cries. The townspeople stood with bundles on their shoulders, ready to flee.

sentences.zh: 高祖率所領奔擊，大破之，投巘赴水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Gaozu led those under his command in a charge and routed them completely; very many were killed casting themselves into gullies or drowning in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu led his men in a charge and broke them completely. Huge numbers were killed falling into ravines or drowning.

sentences.zh: 恩以彭排

translations.literal: En, using a pengpai
translations.idiomatic: En boarded a pengpai

sentences.zh: 〈音敗〉

translations.literal: 〈pronounced bai〉
translations.idiomatic: (pronounced bai)

sentences.zh: 自載，[2]僅得還船。

translations.literal: He carried himself aboard and barely got back to his ship (source note 2).
translations.idiomatic: He boarded a raft under his own power and barely made it back to his ship (source note 2).

sentences.zh: 雖被摧破，猶恃其眾力，徑向京師。

translations.literal: Though shattered, he still relied on the strength of his masses and headed straight for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Though beaten, he still trusted his numbers and steered straight for the capital.

sentences.zh: 樓船高大，值風不得進，旬日乃至白石。

translations.literal: His tower ships were large and tall; meeting contrary winds they could not advance, and only after ten days did they reach Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: His tower ships were huge, but contrary winds held them back, and ten days passed before they reached Baishi.

sentences.zh: 尋知劉牢之已還，朝廷有備，遂走向鬱洲。

translations.literal: Before long he learned that Liu Laozhi had already returned and that the court was prepared, and so he turned toward Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he learned that Laozhi had returned and the court was ready. He turned toward Yuzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 八月，以高祖為建武將軍、下邳太守，領水軍追討至鬱洲，[3]復大破恩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Gaozu was made General Who Establishes Martial Might and Administrator of Xiapi, commanding the navy in pursuit to Yuzhou, [3] and again routed En completely.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Gaozu was appointed General Who Establishes Martial Might and administrator of Xiapi, commanding the navy in pursuit to Yuzhou.[3] He routed En again.

sentences.zh: 恩南走。

translations.literal: En fled south.
translations.idiomatic: En fled south.

sentences.zh: 十一月，高祖追恩於滬瀆，及海鹽，又破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Gaozu pursued En at Hudu and at Haiyan and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Gaozu pursued En to Hudu and Haiyan and defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 三戰並大獲，俘馘以萬數。

translations.literal: In three battles he gained great victories each time, capturing and beheading by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Three great victories in a row brought tens of thousands of prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 恩自是饑饉疾疫，死者太半，自浹口奔臨海。

translations.literal: From then on En suffered famine and pestilence; more than half his men died, and he fled from Jiakou toward Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: After that famine and plague ravaged En's ranks; more than half died, and he fled from Jiakou toward Linhai.

sentences.zh: 元興元年正月，驃騎將軍司馬元顯西伐荊州刺史桓玄，玄亦率荊楚大眾，下討元顯。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yuanxing, General of Agile Cavalry Sima Yuanxian marched west to attack Jingzhou Inspector Huan Xuan; Xuan also led the great host of Jing and Chu downstream to attack Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanxing 1 (402), General of Agile Cavalry Sima Yuanxian marched west against Jingzhou inspector Huan Xuan. Xuan answered with the full strength of Jing and Chu and came downriver against him.

sentences.zh: 元顯遣鎮北將軍劉牢之拒之，高祖參其軍事。

translations.literal: Yuanxian sent Defender of the North Liu Laozhi to oppose him; Gaozu served on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian sent Defender of the North Liu Laozhi to block him. Gaozu served on Laozhi's staff.

sentences.zh: 次溧洲。

translations.literal: They halted at Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The army stopped at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 玄至，高祖請擊之，不許，將遣子敬宣詣玄請和。

translations.literal: When Xuan arrived, Gaozu requested permission to attack him, but it was not granted; they were about to send Jingxuan to Xuan to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan arrived, Gaozu asked to attack and was refused. Laozhi meant to send Jingxuan to Xuan to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 高祖與牢之甥東海何無忌並固諫，不從。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Laozhi's nephew from Donghai, He Wuji, together strongly remonstrated, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Laozhi's nephew He Wuji of Donghai pleaded with him together, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: [4]遂遣敬宣詣玄。

translations.literal: [4] He then sent Jingxuan to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: [4] He sent Jingxuan to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄剋京邑，殺元顯，以牢之為會稽內史。

translations.literal: Xuan took the capital, killed Yuanxian, and made Laozhi Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan seized the capital, killed Yuanxian, and appointed Laozhi interior minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 懼而告高祖曰：「便奪我兵，禍其至矣。

translations.literal: In fear he told Gaozu: "He is about to take my army from me—disaster is at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Laozhi told Gaozu, "He is going to strip me of my troops. Disaster is coming.

sentences.zh: 今當北就高雅於廣陵舉事，卿能從我去乎？

translations.literal: Now I must go north to join Gao Ya at Guangling and raise an army. Can you come away with me?
translations.idiomatic: I must go north to Gao Ya at Guangling and raise troops. Will you come with me?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「將軍以勁卒數萬，望風降服。

translations.literal: " He answered: "The general, with tens of thousands of crack troops, surrendered at the mere rumor of the enemy's approach.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu replied, "You had tens of thousands of elite soldiers, yet you surrendered the moment the enemy drew near.

sentences.zh: 彼新得志，威震天下。

translations.literal: They have newly gained their aim and awe the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They have just seized power and their prestige fills the empire.

sentences.zh: 三軍人情，都已去矣，廣陵豈可得至邪！

translations.literal: The hearts of the Three Armies have already left you—how could you possibly reach Guangling!
translations.idiomatic: Your army's loyalty is already gone. You will never reach Guangling!

sentences.zh: 裕當反服還京口耳。

translations.literal: Yu will simply put on mourning garb and return to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: As for me, I shall put on mourning and go back to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 」牢之叛走自縊死。

translations.literal: " Laozhi fled in rebellion and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Laozhi rebelled, fled, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 何無忌謂高祖曰：「我將何之？

translations.literal: He Wuji said to Gaozu: "Where am I to go?
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji asked Gaozu, "Where should I go?

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「鎮北去必不免，卿可隨我還京口。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "The Defender of the North, if he leaves, will surely not escape death. You may follow me back to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said, "If Laozhi leaves, he cannot live. Come back to Jingkou with me.

sentences.zh: 桓玄必能守節北面，我當與卿事之；

translations.literal: Huan Xuan will surely be able to uphold the rites and face north; I shall then serve him with you;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan may yet observe proper loyalty to the throne, and then you and I can serve him.

sentences.zh: 不然，與卿圖之。

translations.literal: if not, I shall plot against him with you.
translations.idiomatic: If not, we will plot against him together.

sentences.zh: 今方是玄矯情任算之日，必將用我輩也。

translations.literal: Now is precisely the day when Xuan is putting on a show of virtue while calculating his moves; he is sure to make use of us.
translations.idiomatic: This is the moment when Xuan is feigning virtue and scheming. He is bound to employ us.

sentences.zh: 」桓玄從兄脩以撫軍鎮丹徒，以高祖為中兵參軍，軍、郡如故。

translations.literal: " Huan Xuan's older cousin's son Xiu, as Pacifier of the Army, garrisoned Dantu and appointed Gaozu middle army staff officer, his army and commandery posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan's cousin Xiu, holding the post of Pacifier of the Army at Dantu, appointed Gaozu middle-army staff officer with his former military and civil titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 孫恩自奔敗之後，徒旅漸散，懼生見獲，乃於臨海投水死。

translations.literal: After Sun En fled in defeat, his followers gradually dispersed; fearing capture alive, he threw himself into the waters at Linhai and died.
translations.idiomatic: After his final defeat Sun En's followers melted away. Afraid of being taken alive, he drowned himself in the sea off Linhai.

sentences.zh: 餘眾推恩妹夫盧循為主。

translations.literal: The remnant host made En's brother-in-law Lu Xun their leader.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors set up En's brother-in-law Lu Xun as their leader.

sentences.zh: 桓玄欲且緝寧東土，以循為永嘉太守。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan wished for the moment to pacify the eastern lands and appointed Xun Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan wanted peace in the east for the time being and named Xun administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 循雖受命，而寇暴不已。

translations.literal: Though Xun accepted the appointment, his raiding and violence did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Xun accepted the post, but his raids and violence never stopped.

sentences.zh: 五月，玄復遣高祖東征。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xuan again sent Gaozu on an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xuan sent Gaozu east again.

sentences.zh: 時循自臨海入東陽。

translations.literal: At that time Xun had entered Dongyang from Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had come from Linhai into Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，玄復遣高祖破循於東陽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Xuan again sent Gaozu to defeat Xun at Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year (403) Xuan again sent Gaozu, who defeated Xun at Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 循奔永嘉，復追破之，斬其大帥張士道，追討至于晉安，循浮海南走。

translations.literal: Xun fled to Yongjia; Gaozu pursued and defeated him again, beheading his great commander Zhang Shidao, pursuing as far as Jin'an; Xun fled south by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled to Yongjia. Gaozu pursued, beat him again, and beheaded his commander Zhang Shidao, chasing as far as Jin'an before Xun escaped south by sea.

sentences.zh: 六月，加高祖彭城內史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Gaozu was promoted to Interior Minister of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Gaozu was promoted to interior minister of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 桓玄為楚王，將謀篡盜。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan became Prince of Chu and was about to plot usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan became Prince of Chu and prepared to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄從兄衞將軍謙屏人問高祖曰：「楚王勳德隆重，四海歸懷。

translations.literal: Xuan's older cousin's son, Defender-in-Chief Qian, dismissed the others and asked Gaozu: "The Prince of Chu's merit and virtue are weighty, and the realm turns to him in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's cousin Defender-in-Chief Qian sent everyone else away and asked Gaozu, "The Prince of Chu's achievements are immense, and the empire looks to him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷之情，咸謂宜有揖讓，卿意以為何如？

translations.literal: Court opinion everywhere holds that there ought to be a voluntary abdication. What do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion holds there should be a peaceful transfer of the mandate. What is your view?

sentences.zh: 」高祖既志欲圖玄，乃遜辭答曰：「楚王，宣武之子，勳德蓋世。

translations.literal: " Gaozu, who already intended to plot against Xuan, answered with modest words: "The Prince of Chu is the son of Duke Xuanwu; his merit and virtue cover the age.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu already meant to overthrow Xuan, but answered cautiously: "The Prince of Chu is son of Duke Xuanwu. His achievements tower over the age.

sentences.zh: 晉室微弱，民望久移，乘運禪代，有何不可。

translations.literal: The Jin house is feeble; the people's hopes have long shifted. To take the mandate in accord with the times—what could be impossible?
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dynasty is weak and popular allegiance has long since shifted. To accept the mandate when the moment comes—why not?

sentences.zh: 」謙喜曰：「卿謂可爾，便當是真可爾。

translations.literal: " Qian rejoiced and said: "If you say it can be done, then it truly can be done.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian was delighted. "If you say it is possible," he said, "then it truly is possible.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，桓玄篡帝位，遷天子於尋陽。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month, Huan Xuan usurped the imperial throne and moved the Son of Heaven to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month Huan Xuan seized the throne and moved the emperor to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 桓脩入朝，高祖從至京邑。

translations.literal: Huan Xiu entered the court; Gaozu accompanied him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiu went to court, and Gaozu went with him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄見高祖，謂司徒王謐曰：「昨見劉裕，風骨不恒，蓋人傑也。

translations.literal: When Xuan saw Gaozu, he said to Minister of Education Wang Mi: "Yesterday I saw Liu Yu; his bearing is uncommon—surely a hero among men.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan met Gaozu he told Minister of Education Wang Mi, "I saw Liu Yu yesterday. His presence is unlike ordinary men. He is a hero.

sentences.zh: 」每遊集，輒引接慇懃，贈賜甚厚。

translations.literal: " Whenever they met at gatherings, he would draw him close with earnest courtesy and bestow gifts in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever they met at feasts Xuan drew him close with warm courtesy and heaped gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 高祖愈惡之。

translations.literal: Gaozu hated this all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu only hated him the more.

sentences.zh: 或說玄曰：「劉裕龍行虎步，視瞻不凡，恐不為人下，宜蚤為其所。

translations.literal: Someone advised Xuan: "Liu Yu walks like a dragon and tiger; his gaze is extraordinary. I fear he will not remain beneath others—you ought to deal with him early.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Xuan, "Liu Yu moves like a dragon and tiger, and his eyes are unsettling. He will not stay subordinate. You should remove him early.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「我方欲平蕩中原，非劉裕莫可付以大事。

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "I am just about to pacify the Central Plains; there is no one but Liu Yu to whom great affairs can be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan said, "I mean to pacify the Central Plains. No one but Liu Yu can be entrusted with so great a charge.

sentences.zh: 關、隴平定，然後當別議之耳。

translations.literal: When Guan and Long are pacified, then we may discuss the matter separately.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guan and Long are settled, we can speak of this again."

sentences.zh: 」玄乃下詔曰：「劉裕以寡制眾，屢摧妖鋒。

translations.literal: " Xuan then issued an edict saying: "Liu Yu, with few against many, has repeatedly shattered the demonic enemy's point.
translations.idiomatic: " He then issued an edict: "Liu Yu, though outnumbered, has again and again broken the rebel spearhead.

sentences.zh: 汎海窮追，十殄其八。

translations.literal: He pursued them across the sea to the end, destroying eight out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: He chased them across the sea and destroyed eight in ten.

sentences.zh: 諸將力戰，多被重創。

translations.literal: The generals fought fiercely and many suffered grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: His generals fought hard; many were badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 自元帥以下至于將士，並宜論賞，以敍勳烈。」

translations.literal: From the commander-in-chief down to officers and soldiers, all should be rewarded according to merit, to record their achievements."
translations.idiomatic: From the commander down to the common soldier, rewards are due, that their deeds may be recorded."

sentences.zh: 先是高祖東征盧循，何無忌隨至山陰，勸於會稽舉義。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu was on the eastern campaign against Lu Xun, He Wuji followed him to Shanyin and urged raising righteousness in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on the eastern campaign against Lu Xun, He Wuji had gone with Gaozu to Shanyin and urged an uprising in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 高祖以為玄未據極位，且會稽遙遠，事濟為難，俟其篡逆事著，徐於京口圖之，不憂不剋。

translations.literal: Gaozu held that Xuan had not yet reached the supreme position, and that Kuaiji was far away—success would be hard; one should wait until his usurpation was plain, then slowly plot at Jingkou—there was no worry of failure.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thought Xuan had not yet seized the throne, and Kuaiji was too remote for a coup to succeed. Better wait until his treason was obvious, then strike from Jingkou. Victory was certain.

sentences.zh: 至是桓脩還京，高祖託以金創疾動，不堪步從，乃與無忌同船共還，建興復之計。

translations.literal: When Huan Xiu returned to the capital, Gaozu pleaded that a wound from an old blade had flared up and he could not walk in attendance; he and Wuji returned on the same boat and laid plans to restore Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xiu went back to the capital, Gaozu claimed an old war wound had reopened and he could not keep pace on foot. He and Wuji took the same boat home and plotted to restore the Jin.

sentences.zh: 於是與弟道規、沛郡劉毅、平昌孟昶、任城魏詠之、高平檀憑之、琅邪諸葛長民、太原王元德、隴西辛扈興、東莞童厚之，並同義謀。

translations.literal: Thereupon, with his younger brother Daogui, Peijun Liu Yi, Pingchang Meng Chang, Rencheng Wei Yongzhi, Gaoping Tan Pingzhi, Langye Zhuge Changmin, Taiyuan Wang Yuande, Longxi Xin Huxing, and Dongguan Tong Houzhi, he joined in the righteous plot.
translations.idiomatic: He joined his brother Daogui, Liu Yi of Peijun, Meng Chang of Pingchang, Wei Yongzhi of Rencheng, Tan Pingzhi of Gaoping, Zhuge Changmin of Langye, Wang Yuande of Taiyuan, Xin Huxing of Longxi, and Tong Houzhi of Dongguan in a secret league.

sentences.zh: 時桓脩弟弘為征虜將軍、青州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: At that time Xiu's younger brother Hong was General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of Qingzhou, garrisoning Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's brother Hong was then General Who Subdues the Barbarians and inspector of Qingzhou, stationed at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 道規為弘中兵參軍，昶為州主簿。

translations.literal: Daogui served Hong as middle army staff officer; Chang was chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui was on Hong's staff as middle-army officer; Chang was provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 乃令毅潛往就昶，聚徒於江北，謀起兵殺弘。

translations.literal: They then sent Yi secretly to join Chang, gathering followers north of the river and plotting to raise troops and kill Hong.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Yi secretly to Chang to raise men north of the Yangzi and kill Hong.

sentences.zh: 長民為豫州刺史刁逵左軍府參軍，謀據歷陽相應。

translations.literal: Changmin was left army staff officer to Inspector of Yuzhou Diao Kui and plotted to seize Liyang in support.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin, on the staff of Yuzhou inspector Diao Kui, planned to seize Liyang in concert.

sentences.zh: 元德、厚之謀於京邑聚眾攻玄，並剋期齊發。

translations.literal: Yuande and Houzhi plotted to gather masses in the capital to attack Xuan, all fixing the same day to rise together.
translations.idiomatic: Yuande and Houzhi would rally supporters in the capital; every plot fixed the same day to strike.

sentences.zh: 三年二月己丑朔，乙卯，高祖託以遊獵，與無忌等收集義徒，凡同謀何無忌、魏詠之、詠之弟欣之、順之、檀憑之、憑之從子韶、韶弟祗、隆、道濟、[5]道濟從兄範之、高祖弟道憐、劉毅、毅從弟藩、孟昶、昶族弟懷玉、河內向彌、管義之、陳留周安穆、臨淮劉蔚、從弟珪之、東莞臧熹、[6]從弟寶符、從子穆生、童茂宗、陳郡周道民、漁陽田演、譙國范清等二十七人；

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month of the third year, on the day yimao, Gaozu, under pretext of a hunting excursion, gathered righteous followers with Wuji and the rest; the fellow conspirators numbered twenty-seven: He Wuji, Wei Yongzhi, Yongzhi's brothers Xinzhi and Shunzhi, Tan Pingzhi, Pingzhi's cousin Shao, Shao's brothers Zhi, Long, and Daoji, [5] Daoji's cousin Fanzhi, Gaozu's brother Daoling, Liu Yi, Yi's cousin Fan, Meng Chang, Chang's clansman Huaiyu, Henei Xiang Mi, Guan Yizhi, Chenliu Zhou Anmu, Huaiyin Liu Wei, Wei's cousin Guizhi, Dongguan Zang Xi, [6] Xi's cousin Baofu, Xi's nephew Musheng, Tong Maozong, Chenjun Zhou Daomin, Yuyang Tian Yan, and Qiaoguo Fan Qing;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the twenty-eighth day of the second month of the third year (404), Gaozu pretended to go hunting and mustered his allies with Wuji. Twenty-seven men shared the oath: He Wuji, Wei Yongzhi and his brothers Xinzhi and Shunzhi, Tan Pingzhi and his cousin Shao and Shao's brothers Zhi, Long, and Daoji,[5] Daoji's cousin Fanzhi, Gaozu's brother Daoling, Liu Yi and his cousin Fan, Meng Chang and his clansman Huaiyu, Xiang Mi of Henei, Guan Yizhi, Zhou Anmu of Chenliu, Liu Wei of Huaiyin and his cousin Guizhi, Zang Xi of Dongguan,[6] Xi's cousin Baofu and nephew Musheng, Tong Maozong, Zhou Daomin of Chenjun, Tian Yan of Yuyang, and Fan Qing of Qiaoguo;

sentences.zh: 願從者百餘人。

translations.literal: Those willing to follow numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: more than a hundred volunteers came with them.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詰旦，城開，無忌服傳詔服，稱詔居前。

translations.literal: On bingchen, at dawn, the gates opened; Wuji wore robes as if bearing an imperial edict and, proclaiming the edict, went ahead.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on bingchen the gates opened. Wuji dressed as if carrying an imperial order and marched at the head, proclaiming it.

sentences.zh: 義眾馳入，齊聲大呼，吏士驚散，莫敢動，即斬脩以徇。

translations.literal: The righteous host galloped in, shouting together; officials and soldiers were startled and scattered, none daring to move; they at once beheaded Xiu and displayed his head.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels charged in with a great shout. Officials and soldiers scattered in terror. No one resisted. They beheaded Xiu at once and displayed his head.

sentences.zh: 高祖哭甚慟，厚加殯斂。

translations.literal: Gaozu wept bitterly and gave him lavish funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wept bitterly and gave him a lavish funeral—his cousin, after all.

sentences.zh: 孟昶勸弘其日出獵。

translations.literal: Meng Chang urged Hong to go out hunting that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang persuaded Hong to go hunting that same day.

sentences.zh: 未明開門，出獵人，昶、道規、毅等率壯士五六十人因開門直入。

translations.literal: Before dawn the gates opened for the hunting party; Chang, Daogui, Yi, and the rest led fifty or sixty stalwarts through the opened gates straight in.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn the gates opened for the hunt. Chang, Daogui, Yi, and fifty or sixty picked men slipped through and rushed in.

sentences.zh: 弘方噉粥，即斬之，因收眾濟江。

translations.literal: Hong was just eating his porridge when they cut him down; they then gathered the troops and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was at his morning porridge when they killed him. They gathered his troops and crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 義軍初剋京城，脩司馬刁弘率文武佐吏來赴。

translations.literal: When the righteous army first took the capital, Xiu's staff officer Diao Hong led civil and military subordinates to come in submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the loyalists first seized the capital, Xiu's staff officer Diao Hong came with civil and military officials to submit.

sentences.zh: 高祖登城謂之曰：「郭江州已奉乘輿反正於尋陽，我等並被密詔，誅除逆黨，同會今日。

translations.literal: Gaozu mounted the wall and said to him: "Inspector Guo of Jiangzhou has already received the imperial carriage and restored righteousness at Xunyang; we too have all received secret edicts to exterminate the traitorous faction, and we meet on this day.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mounted the wall and told him, "Inspector Guo of Jiangzhou has already received the emperor at Xunyang and declared for the restoration. We too hold secret orders to destroy the traitors. Today we act together.

sentences.zh: 賊玄之首，已當梟於大航矣。

translations.literal: The bandit Xuan's head will soon be displayed on the Great Ferry.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's head will soon hang at the Great Ferry.

sentences.zh: 諸君非大晉之臣乎，今來欲何為？

translations.literal: Are you not ministers of great Jin? What have you come for now?
translations.idiomatic: You are still ministers of Jin. Why have you come?"

sentences.zh: 」弘等信之，收眾而退。

translations.literal: " Hong and the rest believed him and withdrew their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Hong believed him and led his men away.

sentences.zh: 毅既至，高祖命誅弘。

translations.literal: When Yi arrived, Gaozu ordered Hong executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi arrived, Gaozu had Hong executed.

sentences.zh: 毅兄邁先在京師，事未發數日，高祖遣同謀周安穆報之，使為內應。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Mai was already in the capital; several days before the affair broke, Gaozu sent fellow conspirator Zhou Anmu to report to him, that he might serve as inner support.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Mai was already in the capital. Days before the rising Gaozu sent Zhou Anmu to enlist him as an inside man.

sentences.zh: 邁外雖酬許，內甚震懼。

translations.literal: Outwardly Mai answered agreeably, but inwardly he was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Mai agreed outwardly but was terrified within.

sentences.zh: 安穆見其惶駭，慮事必泄，乃馳歸。

translations.literal: Anmu, seeing his panic, feared the affair would leak, and galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Anmu saw his panic, feared a leak, and rode back at speed.

sentences.zh: 時玄以邁為竟陵太守，邁不知所為，便下船欲之郡。

translations.literal: At that time Xuan had made Mai Administrator of Jingling; Mai did not know what to do and boarded a boat to go to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had just made Mai administrator of Jingling. Mai, at a loss, boarded a boat for his post.

sentences.zh: 是夜，玄與邁書曰：「北府人情云何？

translations.literal: That night Xuan wrote to Mai: "What is the mood among the Northern Headquarters men?
translations.idiomatic: That night Xuan wrote to Mai: "What is the mood in the Northern Headquarters?

sentences.zh: 卿近見劉裕何所道？

translations.literal: What did Liu Yu say when you saw him recently?
translations.idiomatic: What did Liu Yu say when you saw him lately?"

sentences.zh: 」邁謂玄已知其謀，晨起白之。

translations.literal: " Mai thought Xuan already knew of the plot; at dawn he went to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Mai thought Xuan already knew. At dawn he went to tell him.

sentences.zh: 玄驚懼，封邁為重安侯；

translations.literal: Xuan was alarmed and afraid; he enfeoffed Mai as Marquis of Chong'an;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was terrified. He enfeoffed Mai as Marquis of Chong'an;

sentences.zh: 既而嫌邁不執安穆，使得逃去，[7]乃殺之。

translations.literal: then, resenting that Mai had not seized Anmu and let him escape, [7] he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: then, angry that Mai had let Anmu escape,[7] killed him.

sentences.zh: 誅元德、扈興、厚之等。

translations.literal: He executed Yuande, Huxing, Houzhi, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Yuande, Huxing, Houzhi, and others caught in the capital.

sentences.zh: 召桓謙、卞範之等謀拒高祖。

translations.literal: He summoned Huan Qian, Bian Fanzhi, and the rest to plan resisting Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He called in Huan Qian, Bian Fanzhi, and others to plan resistance.

sentences.zh: 謙等曰：「亟遣兵擊之。

translations.literal: Qian and the rest said: "Send troops at once to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Qian urged an immediate attack.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "No.

sentences.zh: 彼兵速銳，計出萬死。

translations.literal: Their troops are swift and sharp; their plan is born of desperation.
translations.idiomatic: Their men are fast and fierce, fighting with nothing to lose.

sentences.zh: 若行遣水軍，不足相抗，如有蹉跌，則彼氣成而吾事敗矣。

translations.literal: If we send the navy, it will not be enough to resist them; if there is any slip, their spirit will rise and our cause will fail.
translations.idiomatic: A naval force might not stop them. One setback and their morale will soar while ours collapses.

sentences.zh: 不如屯大眾於覆舟山以待之。

translations.literal: Better mass a great host on Fuzhou Mountain and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Better mass an army on Fuzhou Mountain and wait.

sentences.zh: 彼空行二百里，無所措手，銳氣已挫，既至，忽見大軍，必驚懼駭愕。

translations.literal: They will march two hundred li on empty roads with nowhere to act; their keen edge will already be dulled; when they arrive and suddenly see a great army, they will surely be shocked and dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: They will march two hundred li on empty roads with nowhere to strike. Their edge will dull. When they see a great host, they will panic.

sentences.zh: 我案兵堅陣，勿與交鋒，彼求戰不得，自然散走。

translations.literal: We hold our troops in a firm formation and do not join battle; unable to obtain the fight they seek, they will naturally scatter and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Hold a solid line and refuse battle. Unable to fight, they will melt away.

sentences.zh: 此計之上也。

translations.literal: This is the supreme plan.
translations.idiomatic: That is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 」謙等固請，乃遣頓丘太守吳甫之、右衞將軍皇甫敷北拒義軍。

translations.literal: " Qian and the rest pressed hard, and so he sent Administrator of Dunqiu Wu Fuzhi and Right Defender-in-Chief Huangfu Fu north to resist the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him anyway. He sent Wu Fuzhi, administrator of Dunqiu, and Huangfu Fu, Right Defender-in-Chief, north against the loyalists.

sentences.zh: 玄自聞軍起，憂懼無復為計。

translations.literal: From the moment Xuan heard the army had risen, worry and fear left him no further plan.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment he heard of the rising, Xuan was too frightened to think straight.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「劉裕等眾力甚弱，豈辦之有成，陛下何慮之甚。

translations.literal: Someone said: "Liu Yu and the rest are very weak in numbers—how could they succeed? Why does Your Majesty worry so greatly?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Liu Yu's force is tiny. How can they succeed? Why such fear?

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「劉裕足為一世之雄；

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "Liu Yu is hero enough for an age;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan answered, "Liu Yu is a hero of the age.

sentences.zh: 劉毅家無擔石之儲，摴蒲一擲百萬；

translations.literal: Liu Yi has not a picul of stores at home, yet stakes a million on a single throw of dice;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi has not a picul in his house yet will stake a million on one throw of dice.

sentences.zh: 何無忌，劉牢之甥，酷似其舅。

translations.literal: He Wuji is Liu Laozhi's nephew and is the very image of his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji is Laozhi's nephew and his very image.

sentences.zh: 共舉大事，何謂無成。」

translations.literal: Together they undertake a great affair—how can you say they will not succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Together they attempt a great thing. How can you call them doomed?"

sentences.zh: 眾推高祖為盟主，移檄京邑，曰：

translations.literal: The masses acclaimed Gaozu as league leader; he issued a proclamation to the capital, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The allies made Gaozu their leader. He issued a proclamation to the capital:

sentences.zh: 夫治亂相因，理不常泰，狡焉肆虐，或值聖明。

translations.literal: Order and disorder follow one another; reason does not forever abide in peace; when the cunning run wild, sometimes they meet a sage ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Order and chaos alternate; peace cannot last forever. When the wicked run rampant, a sage ruler may yet appear.

sentences.zh: 自我大晉，陽九屢構，隆安以來，難結皇室，忠臣碎於虎口，貞良弊於豺狼。

translations.literal: Since our great Jin, the yang nine calamities have recurred again and again; since Long'an, troubles have bound the imperial house—loyal ministers shattered at tiger jaws, the upright ruined by wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of Jin, disaster has struck again and again. Since Long'an the throne has been beset—loyal ministers torn by tigers, good men devoured by wolves.

sentences.zh: 逆臣桓玄，陵虐人鬼，阻兵荊郢，肆暴都邑。

translations.literal: The traitor Huan Xuan tyrannized men and ghosts, blocked arms in Jing and Ying, and wantoned in violence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor Huan Xuan oppressed heaven and earth, held Jing and Ying by force, and ravaged the capital.

sentences.zh: 天未亡難，凶力繁興，踰年之間，遂傾皇祚。

translations.literal: Heaven had not yet ended the calamity; his brutal power flourished, and within a year he overturned the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had not yet ended the ordeal, yet his brutal power waxed; within a year he stole the throne.

sentences.zh: 主上播越，流幸非所，神器沉淪，七廟毀墜。

translations.literal: Our lord was driven afar, wandering to places not his own; the sacred vessel sank in the depths, and the seven temples were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was driven into exile; the sacred regalia sank in darkness; the ancestral temples fell in ruin.

sentences.zh: 夏后之罹浞、豷，有漢之遭莽、卓，方之於玄，未足為喻。

translations.literal: The afflictions of Xia Hou at Zhu and Yi, the sufferings of Han at Mang and Zhuo—compared with Xuan, they are not enough for a likeness.
translations.idiomatic: The woes of the Xia at Zhu and Yi, of Han at Mang and Zhuo—Xuan surpasses them all.

sentences.zh: 自玄纂逆，于今歷年，亢旱彌時，民無生氣。

translations.literal: Since Xuan usurped, years have passed; drought has lasted long, and the people have no breath of life.
translations.idiomatic: Since his usurpation years have passed. Drought endures. The people barely breathe.

sentences.zh: 加以士庶疲於轉輸，文武困於造築，父子乖離，室家分散，豈唯大東有杼軸之悲，摽梅有傾筐之塈而已哉。

translations.literal: Moreover, gentry and commoners are worn out by transport levies, civil and military by construction labor; fathers and sons are torn apart, households scattered—is it only the grief of the eastern states at empty looms, or the distress of plums overfilled in baskets?
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners break under transport corvée; officials and soldiers under forced labor. Families split, homes scattered. The eastern provinces weep at empty looms; maidens grieve that their baskets overflow with plums none will take.

sentences.zh: 仰觀天文，俯察人事，此而能久，孰有可亡。

translations.literal: Looking up at the heavens, looking down at human affairs—if this can long endure, what could not perish?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven above and earth below—can such a reign endure? What could not fall?

sentences.zh: 凡在有心，誰不扼腕。

translations.literal: All who have a heart—who does not clench his fist?
translations.idiomatic: Every man with a heart clenches his fist.

sentences.zh: 裕等所以叩心泣血，不遑啟處者也。

translations.literal: This is why Yu and the rest beat their breasts and weep blood, unable to find rest.
translations.idiomatic: That is why we beat our breasts and weep blood and cannot sleep.

sentences.zh: 是故夕寐宵興，援獎忠烈，潛搆崎嶇，險過履虎。

translations.literal: Therefore we rise at night and lie down at dawn, aiding and rewarding the loyal and fierce, secretly building on rugged paths, danger surpassing treading on tigers.
translations.idiomatic: We rise at night and sleep at dawn, rewarding the loyal, stealing along paths more dangerous than walking on tigers.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍劉毅、廣武將軍何無忌、鎮北主簿孟昶、兗州主簿魏詠之、寧遠將軍劉道規、龍驤將軍劉藩、振威將軍檀憑之等，忠烈斷金，精貫白日，荷戈奮袂，志在畢命。

translations.literal: Assistant to the State Liu Yi, General of Broad Martial He Wuji, chief clerk of the Pacifier of the North Meng Chang, chief clerk of Yanzhou Wei Yongzhi, General Who Pacifies the Far Liu Daogui, General of the Dragon Cavalry Liu Fan, General Who Quells the Foe Tan Pingzhi, and the rest—their loyalty severs metal, their spirit pierces the sun; bearing weapons they spring forward, resolved to die to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, He Wuji, Meng Chang, Wei Yongzhi, Liu Daogui, Liu Fan, Tan Pingzhi, and the rest—loyalty that cuts metal, spirit that pierces the sun—take up arms resolved to die.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史毛璩，萬里齊契，掃定荊楚。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Mao Jin, in accord across ten thousand li, sweeps and settles Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jin, inspector of Yizhou, acts in concert from afar to sweep Jing and Chu.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史郭昶之，奉迎主上，宮于尋陽。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiangzhou Guo Chaozhi receives our lord and establishes his palace at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chaozhi of Jiangzhou receives the emperor and lodges him at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 鎮北參軍王元德等，並率部曲，保據石頭。

translations.literal: Staff officer of the Pacifier of the North Wang Yuande and the rest each lead their detachments and hold Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuande and others hold Shitou with their bands.

sentences.zh: 揚武將軍諸葛長民，收集義士，已據歷陽。

translations.literal: General Who Displays Martial Zhuge Changmin has gathered righteous warriors and already holds Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin has gathered loyalists and already holds Liyang.

sentences.zh: 征虜參軍庾賾之等，潛相連結，以為內應。

translations.literal: Staff officer of the Pacifier of the Barbarians Yu Zhenzhi and the rest secretly link together as inner support.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhenzhi and others conspire within as our allies.

sentences.zh: 同力協規，所在蜂起，即日斬偽徐州刺史安城王脩、青州刺史弘首。

translations.literal: Combining strength in one plan, uprisings swarm everywhere; that very day the false Inspector of Xuzhou, Prince of Ancheng Xiu, and Inspector of Qingzhou Hong were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: All rise together. That very day the false inspector of Xuzhou, Prince of Ancheng Xiu, and the inspector of Qingzhou Hong were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 義眾既集，文武爭先，咸謂不有一統，則事無以輯。

translations.literal: The righteous masses having assembled, civil and military vie to be first; all say that without a single command, affairs cannot be brought together.
translations.idiomatic: With the loyal host assembled, civil and military men insist that without one commander the cause cannot hold.

sentences.zh: 裕辭不獲已，遂總軍要。

translations.literal: Yu declined but could not refuse and therefore took overall military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yu declined until he could refuse no longer, and took supreme command.

sentences.zh: 庶上憑祖宗之靈，下罄義夫之力，剪馘逋逆，蕩清京輦。

translations.literal: We look above to the spirits of the ancestors and below to exhaust the strength of the righteous, to cut down and destroy the fleeing traitors and sweep clear the capital.
translations.idiomatic: We trust in the ancestors above and the courage of our men below to cut down the rebels and cleanse the capital.

sentences.zh: 公侯諸君，或世樹忠貞，或身荷爵寵，而並俛眉猾豎，自効莫由，顧瞻周道，寧不弔乎！

translations.literal: Lords and nobles, you who for generations planted loyal purity, or yourselves bore rank and favor, yet all bow your brows to the vicious upstart with no way to show loyalty—gazing on the Zhou way, can you not mourn!
translations.idiomatic: You lords who for generations served in loyalty, or who yourselves received grace—yet bow to this usurper with no way to serve the throne—looking on the way of Zhou, do you not grieve?

sentences.zh: 今日之舉，良其會也。

translations.literal: Today's rising is truly the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Today is the day to act.

sentences.zh: 裕以虛薄，才非古人，勢接於已踐之機，受任於既頹之運。

translations.literal: Yu, shallow and slight, lacks the talent of men of old; the momentum meets a moment already trodden, and the charge comes in a destiny already failing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu is slight in talent, no match for the ancients. Fortune offers a path already half-won; the mandate comes when the dynasty is already failing.

sentences.zh: 丹誠未宣，感慨憤躍，望霄漢以永懷，眄山川以增厲。

translations.literal: My red heart is not yet declared; stirred by feeling I leap in anger, gazing at the Milky Way with everlasting longing, scanning mountains and rivers to increase my resolve.
translations.idiomatic: My heart is not yet spoken; I burn with anger, gaze at the Milky Way and long, look on mountains and rivers and harden my will.

sentences.zh: 授檄之日，神馳賊廷。

translations.literal: On the day the proclamation is issued, my spirit flies to the traitor's court.
translations.idiomatic: On the day this proclamation goes forth, my spirit flies to the traitor's court.

sentences.zh: 以孟昶為長史，總攝後事；

translations.literal: Meng Chang was made chief of staff to oversee rear affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang was made chief of staff to manage the rear;

sentences.zh: 檀憑之為司馬。

translations.literal: Tan Pingzhi was made marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Pingzhi was made marshal.

sentences.zh: 百姓願從者千餘人。

translations.literal: Common people willing to follow numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand commoners joined them.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午朔，遇吳甫之於江乘。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, wuwu, they met Wu Fuzhi at Jiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month they met Wu Fuzhi at Jiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 甫之，玄驍將也，其兵甚銳。

translations.literal: Fuzhi was a fierce general of Xuan; his troops were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi was one of Xuan's fiercest generals; his men fought well.

sentences.zh: 高祖躬執長刀，大呼以衝之，眾皆披靡，即斬甫之。

translations.literal: Gaozu himself grasped a long blade, shouted loudly, and charged them; all were overthrown, and Fuzhi was beheaded at once.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu took a long saber, shouted, and charged. The enemy broke. He cut down Fuzhi on the spot.

sentences.zh: 進至羅落橋，皇甫敷率數千人逆戰。

translations.literal: Advancing to Luoluo Bridge, Huangfu Fu led several thousand men to oppose them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on to Luoluo Bridge. Huangfu Fu met them with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 寧遠將軍檀憑之與高祖各御一隊，憑之戰敗見殺，其眾退散。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Far Tan Pingzhi and Gaozu each commanded a column; Pingzhi was defeated in battle and killed, and his troops scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Pingzhi and Gaozu each led a wing. Pingzhi was killed and his men scattered.

sentences.zh: 高祖進戰彌厲，前後奮擊，應時摧破，即斬敷首。

translations.literal: Gaozu pressed the battle ever more fiercely, striking before and behind; the enemy was shattered at once, and Fu's head was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu fought all the harder, striking on every side. The enemy shattered. Fu was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 初高祖與何無忌等共建大謀，有善相者相高祖及無忌等並當大貴，其應甚近，惟云憑之無相。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu and He Wuji and the rest together formed the great plot, a skilled physiognomist had read Gaozu and Wuji and the rest as all destined for great nobility, the fulfillment very near; only Pingzhi, he said, had no such aspect.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was first laid, a physiognomist had read Gaozu, Wuji, and the rest as all destined for great rank, and soon. Only Pingzhi, he said, lacked the signs.

sentences.zh: 高祖與無忌密相謂曰：「吾等既為同舟，理無偏異。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Wuji secretly said to each other: "We are in the same boat; reason admits no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Wuji whispered together, "We share one boat. Fortune cannot favor some and not others.

sentences.zh: 吾徒咸皆富貴，則檀不應獨殊。

translations.literal: If we are all to be rich and noble, Tan should not alone be unlike the rest.
translations.idiomatic: If we are all to rise, Tan cannot be left out."

sentences.zh: 」深不解相者之言。

translations.literal: " They deeply did not understand the physiognomist's words.
translations.idiomatic: They could not understand the seer.

sentences.zh: 至是而憑之戰死，高祖知其事必捷。

translations.literal: When Pingzhi fell in battle, Gaozu knew the affair would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingzhi fell, Gaozu knew victory was certain.

sentences.zh: 玄聞敷等並沒，愈懼。

translations.literal: When Xuan heard that Fu and the rest were all destroyed, he grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Fu was dead, Xuan grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 使桓謙屯東陵口，卞範之屯覆舟山西，眾合二萬。

translations.literal: He had Huan Qian encamp at Dongling Pass and Bian Fanzhi at the west of Fuzhou Mountain; their forces together numbered twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Huan Qian at Dongling Pass and Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou Mountain—twenty thousand men between them.

sentences.zh: 己未旦，義軍食畢，棄其餘糧，進至覆舟山東，使丐士張旗幟於山上，以為疑兵。

translations.literal: On the morning of jiwei, after the righteous army had eaten, they cast aside their remaining grain, advanced to the east of Fuzhou Mountain, and had beggars raise banners on the hill as a feint.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jiwei the loyalists ate, left their spare grain, and marched east of Fuzhou Mountain, where beggars raised banners on the heights as a decoy.

sentences.zh: 玄又遣武騎將軍庾禕之，[8]配以精卒利器，助謙等。

translations.literal: Xuan also sent General of Martial Cavalry Yu Yizhi, [8] providing elite troops and sharp weapons to aid Qian and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan also sent Yu Yizhi, General of Martial Cavalry,[8] with picked troops and fine arms to reinforce Qian.

sentences.zh: 高祖躬先士卒以奔之，將士皆殊死戰，無不一當百，呼聲動天地。

translations.literal: Gaozu himself took the lead among the soldiers and charged them; officers and men all fought as if ready to die, none not matching one against a hundred; their shouts shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu led the charge himself. His men fought as if death meant nothing, each worth a hundred. Their roar shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 時東北風急，因命縱火，煙爓張天，鼓噪之音震京邑。

translations.literal: At that time a fierce northeast wind blew; he therefore ordered fire set; smoke and flames filled the sky, and the din of drums and shouts shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce northeast wind rose. He ordered the fire lit. Smoke blotted out the sky; drums and war cries shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 謙等諸軍，一時土崩。

translations.literal: Qian and the various armies at once collapsed like earth.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's lines collapsed at once.

sentences.zh: 玄始雖遣軍置陣，而走意已決，別使領軍將軍殷仲文具舟於石頭，仍將子姪浮江南走。

translations.literal: Though Xuan had earlier sent troops to set battle lines, his mind to flee was already fixed; he separately had Defender-in-Chief Yin Zhongwen prepare boats at Shitou, and then led his sons and nephews south across the river by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had drawn up his army, but he meant to run. He had Yin Zhongwen ready boats at Shitou, then fled south across the Yangzi with his kin.

sentences.zh: 庚申，高祖鎮石頭城，立留臺官，[9]焚桓溫神主於宣陽門外，造晉新主，立于太廟。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Gaozu garrisoned Shitou, established the officials of the rear court, [9] burned Huan Wen's spirit tablet outside Xuanyang Gate, and made a new Jin spirit tablet, setting it up in the Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Gaozu held Shitou, set up a provisional government,[9] burned Huan Wen's tablet outside Xuanyang Gate, and installed a new spirit tablet for Jin in the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 遣諸將帥追玄，尚書王嘏率百官奉迎乘輿。

translations.literal: He sent the various generals to pursue Xuan; Minister of the Interior Wang Dan led the hundred officials to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He sent generals in pursuit. Wang Dan of the Ministry of the Interior led the officials to welcome the emperor.

sentences.zh: [10]司徒王謐與眾議推高祖領揚州，固辭。

translations.literal: [10] Minister of Education Wang Mi, with the multitude in counsel, urged Gaozu to take charge of Yangzhou; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: [10] Wang Mi and others urged Gaozu to take Yangzhou. He refused.

sentences.zh: 乃以謐為錄尚書事，領揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Mi was then made Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing and took charge of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was made Recorder of the Masters of Writing and given Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是推高祖為使持節、都督揚、徐、兗、豫、青、冀、幽、并八州諸軍事、領軍將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gaozu was promoted to Bearer of the Staff, Commander over the military affairs of the eight provinces Yang, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, Ji, You, and Bing, Defender-in-Chief, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then appointed bearer of the staff, commander over eight provinces, Defender-in-Chief, and inspector of Xuzhou.

translations.literal: Annotation marker 11.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 11.

sentences.zh: 先是朝廷承晉氏亂政，百司縱弛，桓玄雖欲釐整，而眾莫從之。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had inherited Jin disorder in government; the hundred offices were lax; though Huan Xuan wished to put things in order, none followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court had long been corrupt and offices slack. Xuan tried to reform them, but none obeyed.

sentences.zh: 高祖以身範物，先以威禁內外，百官皆肅然奉職，二三日間，風俗頓改。

translations.literal: Gaozu took his person as a model for things; first he imposed awe and prohibition within and without; the hundred offices all respectfully performed their duties; within two or three days, customs suddenly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu led by example, imposing discipline inside and out. Within days every office snapped to order and customs changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 且桓玄雖以雄豪見推，而一朝便有極位，晉氏四方牧守及在朝大臣，盡心伏事，臣主之分定矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Huan Xuan was promoted as a bold hero, in a single morning he reached the utmost rank; Jin's regional governors on the four sides and great ministers at court all bent their hearts in service—the distinction of minister and lord was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had risen in a day to supreme power; every governor and court minister had submitted. The hierarchy seemed settled.

sentences.zh: 高祖位微於朝，眾無一旅，奮臂草萊之中，倡大義以復皇祚。

translations.literal: Gaozu's rank in court was slight, and he had not a single brigade; he raised his arm from among the grass and weeds, initiating great righteousness to restore the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had been a nobody with barely a company. He raised the banner of restoration from the grass roots.

sentences.zh: 由是王謐等諸人時失民望，[12]莫不愧而憚焉。

translations.literal: Thereby Wang Mi and the rest, who at the time had lost the people's regard, [12] were all ashamed and in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi and the grandees, who had lost the people's trust,[12] were ashamed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 諸葛長民失期不得發，刁逵執送之，未至而玄敗。

translations.literal: Zhuge Changmin missed the appointed day and could not set out; Diao Kui seized and sent him on; before he arrived, Xuan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin missed his rendezvous and was seized by Diao Kui. Before he reached the field, Xuan was already beaten.

sentences.zh: 玄經尋陽，江州刺史郭昶之備乘輿法物資之。

translations.literal: Xuan passed Xunyang; Inspector of Jiangzhou Guo Chaozhi prepared the imperial regalia and supplied him.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Xunyang, Xuan was supplied with imperial regalia by Guo Chaozhi, inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 玄收略得二千餘人，挾天子走江陵。

translations.literal: Xuan gathered about two thousand more men, took the Son of Heaven, and fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He scraped together two thousand more men, seized the emperor, and fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍劉毅、輔國將軍何無忌、振武將軍劉道規率諸軍追討。

translations.literal: Champion General Liu Yi, Assistant to the State He Wuji, and General Who Quells the Foe Liu Daogui led the armies in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, He Wuji, and Liu Daogui led the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射王愉、愉子荊州刺史綏等，江左冠族。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu and Yu's son, Inspector of Jingzhou Sui, were leading clans of the eastern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and his son Sui, inspector of Jingzhou, were great eastern clansmen.

sentences.zh: 綏少有重名，以高祖起自布衣，甚相凌忽。

translations.literal: Sui had a heavy reputation from youth and, because Gaozu rose from common cloth, greatly looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was proud of his name and despised Gaozu as a man risen from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 綏，桓氏甥，亦有自疑之志。

translations.literal: Sui, a nephew of the Huan clan, also harbored doubts of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was Huan Xuan's nephew by marriage and nursed his own suspicions.

sentences.zh: 高祖悉誅之。

translations.literal: Gaozu executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 四月，奉武陵王遵為大將軍，承制。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Prince of Wuling Zun was honored as Grand General and received the mandate to act.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Prince Zun of Wuling was made Grand General with power to act by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下，唯桓玄一祖後不在赦例。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed for the realm; only the descendants of Huan Xuan's one ancestral line were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was amnestied, except for the house of Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 初高祖家貧，嘗負刁逵社錢三萬，經時無以還。

translations.literal: Earlier Gaozu's family was poor; he once owed Diao Kui thirty thousand in community funds and for a long time had no means to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had once been poor and owed Diao Kui thirty thousand in community funds, long unpaid.

sentences.zh: 逵執錄甚嚴，王謐造逵見之，密以錢代還，由是得釋。

translations.literal: Kui's seizure and record were very strict; Wang Mi went to see Kui in secret and repaid the money on his behalf, and thereby he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Kui pressed him hard. Wang Mi secretly repaid the debt for him and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 高祖名微位薄，盛流皆不與相知，唯謐交焉。

translations.literal: Gaozu's name was slight and his rank thin; the great currents all would not know him—only Mi was intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was unknown to the elite; only Mi befriended him.

sentences.zh: 桓玄將篡，謐手解安帝璽紱，為玄佐命功臣。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was about to usurp, Mi with his own hand removed Emperor An's seal and cord and became a meritorious minister aiding Xuan's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan prepared to usurp, Mi himself removed the emperor's seal and cord and served as his chief accomplice.

sentences.zh: 及義旗建，眾並謂謐宜誅，唯高祖保持之。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, all said Mi ought to be executed; only Gaozu protected him.
translations.idiomatic: When the loyalists rose, all demanded Mi's death. Gaozu alone shielded him.

sentences.zh: 劉毅嘗因朝會，問謐璽紱所在，謐益懼。

translations.literal: Liu Yi once at a court assembly asked Mi where the seal and cord were; Mi grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At court Liu Yi once demanded where the imperial seal was. Mi grew terrified.

sentences.zh: 及王愉父子誅，謐從弟諶謂謐曰：「王駒無罪，而義旗誅之，此是剪除勝己，以絕民望。

translations.literal: When Wang Yu and his son were executed, Mi's cousin Zhen said to Mi: "Wang Ju was innocent, yet the righteous army executed him—this is cutting down those who surpass them, to cut off the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Yu and his son died, Mi's cousin Zhen warned him: "Ju was innocent, yet they killed him—to cut down any rival. You are Huan's man, with rank like yours—do you think you can escape?"

sentences.zh: 兄既桓氏黨附，名位如此，欲求免得乎？

translations.literal: You are attached to the Huan party, and your name and rank are such—can you seek to escape unscathed?
translations.idiomatic: You are Huan's ally at such rank. Do you expect mercy?

sentences.zh: 」駒，愉小字也。

translations.literal: " Ju was Wang Yu's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: "Ju was Yu's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 謐懼，奔于曲阿。

translations.literal: Mi, afraid, fled to Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fled in terror to Qu'e.

sentences.zh: 高祖牋白大將軍，深相保謐，迎還復位。

translations.literal: Gaozu memorialized the Grand General, strongly guaranteeing Mi, welcomed him back, and restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu memorialized the Grand General, vouched for Mi, and brought him back to office.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳卞承之、[13]左衞將軍褚粲、游擊將軍司馬秀役使官人，為御史中丞王禎之所糾察，謝牋言辭怨憤。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Household Bian Chengzhi, [13] Left Defender-in-Chief Chu Can, and Mobile Corps General Sima Xiu employed officials for private service; Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhen investigated them; their memorials of apology were resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Chengzhi,[13] Chu Can, and Sima Xiu abused subordinates. Wang Zhen the censor exposed them; their apologies were full of resentment.

sentences.zh: 承之造司宜藏。

translations.literal: Chengzhi went to the judicial office to be imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi was sent to prison.

sentences.zh: 高祖與大將軍牋，白「粲等備位大臣，所懷必盡。

translations.literal: Gaozu memorialized the Grand General, stating: "Can and the rest hold ministerial rank and ought to speak their minds fully.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wrote the Grand General: "Can and the others are great ministers and should speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 執憲不允，自應據理陳訴，而橫興怨忿，歸咎有司。

translations.literal: The law officers were not fair; they should have stated their case according to reason, yet they gave way to resentment and blamed the officials.
translations.idiomatic: If the censors were wrong they should argue the law, not rage at the bench.

sentences.zh: 宜加裁當，以清風軌」。

translations.literal: They should receive appropriate discipline to clear court standards."
translations.idiomatic: Discipline them and restore order."

sentences.zh: 並免官。

translations.literal: All were removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: All were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 桓玄兄子歆，[14]聚眾向歷陽，高祖命輔國將軍諸葛長民擊走之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan's elder brother's son Xin, [14] gathered troops and marched on Liyang; Gaozu ordered Assistant to the State Zhuge Changmin to strike and drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's nephew Xin[14] raised troops toward Liyang. Gaozu sent Changmin and routed him.

sentences.zh: 無忌、道規破玄大將郭銓等于桑落洲，[15]眾軍進據尋陽。

translations.literal: Wuji and Daogui defeated Xuan's great general Guo Qian and the rest at Sangluo Isle, [15] and the armies advanced and occupied Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and Daogui destroyed Guo Qian at Sangluo Isle.[15] The army took Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 加高祖都督江州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Gaozu was promoted to Commander over the military affairs of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made commander over Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 玄既還荊郢，大聚兵眾，召水軍造樓船、器械，率眾二萬，挾天子發江陵，浮江東下，與冠軍將軍劉毅等相遇於崢嶸洲，眾軍下擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Xuan, having returned to Jing and Ying, gathered a great host, summoned the navy to build tower ships and engines, led twenty thousand men, took the Son of Heaven, and set out from Jiangling, floating downstream; he met Champion General Liu Yi and the rest at Zhengrong Isle; the armies struck from below and routed him completely.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Jing and Ying, Xuan built a fleet, mustered twenty thousand men, seized the emperor, and sailed east. Liu Yi met him at Zhengrong Isle and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: [16]玄棄眾，復挾天子還復江陵。

translations.literal: [16] Xuan abandoned his troops, again took the Son of Heaven, and returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: [16] Xuan abandoned his army, seized the emperor again, and fled back to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 玄黨殷仲文奉晉二皇后還京師。

translations.literal: Xuan's partisan Yin Zhongwen escorted the two Jin empresses back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongwen, Xuan's ally, sent the two empresses back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄至江陵，因西走。

translations.literal: When Xuan reached Jiangling, he then fled west.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling Xuan turned west and ran.

sentences.zh: 南郡太守王騰之、荊州別駕王康產奉天子入南郡府。

translations.literal: Administrator of Nanjun Wang Tengzhi and Assistant Administrator of Jingzhou Wang Kangchan received the Son of Heaven into the Nanjun government seat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tengzhi of Nanjun and Wang Kangchan welcomed the emperor into the Nanjun yamen.

sentences.zh: 初征虜將軍、益州刺史毛璩，遣從孫祐之與參軍費恬送弟喪下，有眾二百。

translations.literal: Earlier General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of Yizhou Mao Jin had sent his younger cousin Youzhi and staff officer Fei Tian to escort his younger brother's coffin downstream, with a force of two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jin of Yizhou had sent his cousin Youzhi and Fei Tian with two hundred men to escort a coffin downstream.

sentences.zh: 璩弟子脩之時為玄屯騎校尉，[17]誘玄以入蜀。

translations.literal: Jin's nephew Xiuzhi was then Xuan's Colonel of Valiant Cavalry, [17] and urged Xuan to enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's nephew Xiuzhi, Xuan's colonel,[17] urged him into Shu.

sentences.zh: 至枚回洲，恬與祐之迎射之。

translations.literal: At Meihui Isle, Tian and Youzhi met him with arrows.
translations.idiomatic: At Meihui Isle Tian and Youzhi ambushed him with bowshot.

sentences.zh: 益州督護馮遷斬玄首，傳京師。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Yizhou Feng Qian cut off Xuan's head and sent it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian, Jin's supervisor, cut off Xuan's head and sent it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又斬玄子昇於江陵市。

translations.literal: He also beheaded Xuan's son Sheng in the Jiangling market.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's son Sheng was beheaded in the Jiangling market.

sentences.zh: 初玄敗於崢嶸洲，義軍以為大事已定，追躡不速。

translations.literal: When Xuan was first defeated at Zhengrong Isle, the righteous army thought the great affair was already settled and did not pursue swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhengrong Isle the loyalists thought the war was won and pursued slowly.

sentences.zh: 玄死幾一旬，眾軍猶不至。

translations.literal: Xuan had been dead nearly ten days before the armies still did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten days passed after Xuan's death before the army came up.

sentences.zh: 玄從子振逃於華容之涌中，[18]招聚逆黨數千人，晨襲江陵城，居民競出赴之。

translations.literal: Xuan's nephew Zhen fled into the marshes of Huarong, [18] gathered several thousand traitorous partisans, and at dawn raided Jiangling; the inhabitants rushed out to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's nephew Zhen hid in the Huarong marshes,[18] gathered thousands of rebels, and at dawn stormed Jiangling. The people rushed to join him.

sentences.zh: 騰之、康產皆被殺。

translations.literal: Tengzhi and Kangchan were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tengzhi and Kangchan were killed.

sentences.zh: 桓謙先匿於沮川，亦聚眾以應。

translations.literal: Huan Qian had earlier hidden in Juchuan and also gathered troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian, in hiding at Juchuan, also raised men.

sentences.zh: 振為玄舉哀，立喪廷。

translations.literal: Zhen held mourning for Xuan and set up the mourning hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen mourned Xuan and set up a funeral hall.

sentences.zh: 謙率眾官奉璽綬于安帝。

translations.literal: Qian led the officials to present the seal and cord to Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: Qian led the officials to return the seal and cord to Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 無忌、道規既至江陵，與桓振戰于靈溪。

translations.literal: When Wuji and Daogui reached Jiangling, they fought Zhen at Lingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and Daogui fought Zhen at Lingxi.

sentences.zh: 玄黨馮該又設伏于楊林，義軍奔敗，退還尋陽。

translations.literal: Xuan's partisan Feng Gai again set an ambush at Yanglin; the righteous army was routed in flight and withdrew to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Gai ambushed them at Yanglin. The loyalists were beaten back to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史辛禺懷貳。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Xin Yu harbored double loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yu, inspector of Yanzhou, wavered in his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 會北青州刺史劉該反，禺求征該，次淮陰，又反。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Qingzhou in the north Liu Gai rebelled, Yu requested to campaign against Gai, halted at Huaiyin, and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Gai of Qingzhou rebelled, Yu asked to suppress him, stopped at Huaiyin, and rebelled in turn.

sentences.zh: 禺長史羊穆之斬禺，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Yu's chief clerk Yang Muzhi beheaded Yu and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk Yang Muzhi killed him and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，高祖領青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Gaozu took charge of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gaozu took Qingzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 甲仗百人入殿。

translations.literal: A hundred armored men entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred armored guards entered the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 劉毅諸軍復進至夏口。

translations.literal: Liu Yi and the armies again advanced to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi advanced again to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 毅攻魯城，道規攻偃月壘，皆拔之。

translations.literal: Yi attacked Lucheng; Daogui attacked Yanyue fortress; both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took Lucheng; Daogui took Yanyue fortress.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諸軍進平巴陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the armies advanced and pacified Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they pacified Baling.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年正月，毅等至江津，破桓謙、桓振，江陵平，天子反正。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yixi, Yi and the rest reached Jiangjin, defeated Huan Qian and Huan Zhen, pacified Jiangling, and the Son of Heaven was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yixi 1 (405) the army reached Jiangjin, defeated Qian and Zhen, pacified Jiangling, and the emperor was restored.

sentences.zh: 三月，天子至自江陵。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Son of Heaven arrived from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor returned from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 古稱大者天地，其次君臣，所以列貫三辰，神人代序，諒理本於造昧，而運周於萬葉。

translations.literal: Antiquity says the greatest are Heaven and Earth, next lord and minister; thereby the three luminaries are arrayed, spirits and men succeed one another in order—surely reason roots in primordial obscurity, yet fortune cycles through ten thousand leaves.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients ranked Heaven and Earth first, lord and minister next. Thus the three lights run their course and gods and men take turns in rule—reason lies in the beginning of darkness, yet fortune turns through endless generations.

sentences.zh: 故盈否時襲，四靈通其變，王道或昧，貞賢拯其危，天命所以永固，人心所以攸穆。

translations.literal: Therefore fullness and denial visit in season; the four numina communicate their changes; when the royal way is dim, the steadfast and worthy rescue its peril—the Mandate is thereby made everlasting, and human hearts thereby kept tranquil.
