translations.idiomatic: Fortune and ruin come in seasons; the four spirits shift with them. When the royal way fails, loyal men save it—the Mandate endures and hearts find peace.

sentences.zh: 雖夏、周中傾，賴靡、申之績，莽、倫載竊，實二代是維。

translations.literal: Though Xia and Zhou stumbled mid-course, they relied on the achievements of Mi and Shen; though Mang and Lun briefly stole the throne, the two dynasties were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Xia and Zhou faltered yet were saved by Mi and Shen; usurpers Mang and Lun stole the throne yet the dynasties survived.

sentences.zh: 或乘資藉號，或業隆異世，猶詩書以之休詠，記策用為美談。

translations.literal: Some rode opportunity to take titles, some flourished in another age—still the Odes and Documents praise them, and records make them fine tales.
translations.idiomatic: Some seized the moment, some flourished in another age—yet poetry praises them and histories tell their tales.

sentences.zh: 未有因心撫民，而誠發理應，援神器於已淪，若在今之盛者也。

translations.literal: Never has one who, from the heart, comforted the people, with sincerity answering reason, drawn the sacred vessel from ruin, as in today's splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Never has one who truly comforted the people and restored the sacred vessel from ruin shone as brightly as today.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，遭家不造，越自遘閔，屬當屯極。

translations.literal: We, slight and dim, met with an unlucky house; crossing from misfortune, we came to the utmost of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: We are slight and unlucky, born to a house in ruin, brought to the depths of calamity.

sentences.zh: 逆臣桓玄，乘釁縱慝，窮凶恣虐，滔天猾夏。

translations.literal: The traitor Huan Xuan seized the opportunity and indulged wickedness, to the utmost of cruelty and tyranny, flooding heaven with his violence.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor Huan Xuan seized his chance and ran wild, cruel beyond measure, drowning the realm in blood.

sentences.zh: 遂誣罔人神，肆其篡亂。

translations.literal: He deceived and misled men and spirits and wantoned in usurpation and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He deceived gods and men and usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之基既湮，七廟之饗胥殄，若墜淵谷，未足斯譬。

translations.literal: The ancestors' foundation was drowned; the seven temples' offerings were all cut off—like falling into a deep ravine, not enough for a likeness.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral foundation sank; the seven temples went hungry—like falling into an abyss, words fail.

sentences.zh: 皇度有晉，天縱英哲，使持節、都督揚徐兗豫青冀幽并江九州諸軍事、鎮軍將軍、徐青二州刺史，忠誠天亮，神武命世，用能貞明協契，義夫響臻。

translations.literal: The royal Jin has Heaven's support and an heroic sage: Bearer of the Staff, Commander over the military affairs of the nine provinces Yang, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, Ji, You, Bing, and Jiang, General Who Pacifies the Army, Inspector of Xu and Qing—loyalty bright as heaven, martial spirit commanding the age—thereby able to keep faith with bright accord; righteous men answered his call.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin has Heaven's favor and a hero: bearer of the staff, commander of nine provinces, General Who Pacifies the Army—loyal as daylight, martial as fate—men of righteousness flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 故順聲一唱，二溟卷波，英風振路，宸居清翳。

translations.literal: Therefore at one call the two seas rolled in waves; heroic wind shook the road; the imperial seat was cleared of gloom.
translations.idiomatic: At his call the realm surged like the sea; his fame cleared the throne of shadow.

sentences.zh: 暨冠軍將軍毅、輔國將軍無忌、振武將軍道規，舟旗遄邁，而元凶傳首，回戈疊揮，則荊、漢霧廓。

translations.literal: Then Champion General Yi, Assistant to the State Wuji, and General Who Quells the Foe Daogui—ships and banners flew swiftly, and the arch-traitor's head was passed along; turning spears again and again, Jing and Han were cleared of mist.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Wuji, and Daogui swept downriver; the traitor's head was taken; Jing and Han were cleared.

sentences.zh: 俾宣、元之祚，永固於嵩、岱，傾基重造，再集於朕躬。

translations.literal: Thus the fortunes of Xuan and Yuan are forever fixed on Song and Dai; the leaning foundation was heavily rebuilt and gathered again in Our person.
translations.idiomatic: The fortunes of Jin are secured again on sacred mountains; the throne is rebuilt in our hands.

sentences.zh: 宗廟歆七百之祜，皇基融載新之命。

translations.literal: The ancestral temples enjoy seven hundred years of blessing; the imperial foundation melts and bears the new Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The temples breathe again; the throne receives a new Mandate.

sentences.zh: 念功惟德，永言銘懷。

translations.literal: Thinking of merit, virtue is forever engraved in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: His merit will be remembered forever.

sentences.zh: 固已道冠開闢，獨絕終古，書契以來，未之前聞矣。

translations.literal: Already his Way crowns the opening of the age, alone unmatched through antiquity; since writing began, none has been heard of before.
translations.idiomatic: His achievement crowns the age, unmatched since records began.

sentences.zh: 雖則功高靡尚，理至難文，而崇庸命德，哲王攸先者，將以弘道制治，深關盛衰。

translations.literal: Though merit is high beyond compare and reason hard to phrase, yet exalting merit and appointing virtue—the wise kings put first—is to spread the Way, govern order, and bind closely to rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Though words cannot compass such merit, wise kings reward virtue to bind fortune to the state.

sentences.zh: 故伊、望膺殊命之錫，桓、文饗備物之禮，況宏徵不世，顧邈百代者，宜極名器之隆，以光大國之盛。

translations.literal: Therefore Yi and Wang received extraordinary gifts; Huan and Wen enjoyed rites of full regalia; how much more when the great sign is not of the age and looks across a hundred generations—one should raise name and vessel to the utmost, to enlarge the splendor of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Wang received extraordinary gifts; Huan and Wen full honors—how much more this man, who spans the ages—should receive the highest rank to glorify the realm.

sentences.zh: 而鎮軍謙虛自衷，誠旨屢顯，朕重逆仲父，乃所以愈彰德美也。

translations.literal: Yet the Pacifier of the Army is modest from the heart; his sincere intent has repeatedly appeared; We, heavily going against the second father, thereby only make the virtue shine the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifier of the Army is modest, refusing again and again; by pressing him we only show his virtue the brighter.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍可進位侍中、車騎將軍、都督中外諸軍事，使持節、徐、青二州刺史如故。

translations.literal: The Pacifier of the Army may advance to Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander over all military affairs within and without the seas, Bearer of the Staff, Inspector of Xu and Qing, as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Pacifier of the Army be Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, commander of all armies, bearer of the staff, inspector of Xu and Qing, as before.

sentences.zh: 顯祚大邦，啟茲疆宇。

translations.literal: Manifest fortune in a great state; open this frontier.
translations.idiomatic: May his fortune enlarge the state and open new borders.

sentences.zh: 高祖固讓。

translations.literal: Gaozu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 加錄尚書事，又不受，屢請歸藩。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Recorder of the Masters of Writing; again he did not accept, repeatedly requesting to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: They made him Recorder of the Masters of Writing; he refused again and asked to retire to his fief.

sentences.zh: 天子不許，遣百僚敦勸，又親幸公第。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven did not permit it; he sent the hundred officials to urge him earnestly, and also personally visited his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not allow it, sent officials to urge him, and visited his house in person.

sentences.zh: 高祖惶懼詣闕陳請，天子不能奪。

translations.literal: Gaozu, fearful, went to the palace to state his plea; the Son of Heaven could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu went to court in feigned alarm to plead his case; the emperor could not refuse him.

sentences.zh: 是月，旋鎮丹徒。

translations.literal: That month he returned to garrison Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: That month he withdrew to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 天子重遣大使敦勸，又不受。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again sent a grand envoy to urge him earnestly; again he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent another grand envoy; again Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 乃改授都督荊、司、梁、益、寧、雍、涼七州，并前十六州諸軍事，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was then reassigned as Commander over the military affairs of the seven provinces Jing, Si, Liang, Yi, Ning, Yong, and Liang, together with the former sixteen provinces, his original posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was given command over seven more provinces on top of his sixteen, with all other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 於是受命解青州，加領兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon, accepting the mandate, he relinquished Qingzhou and was additionally given charge of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted, gave up Qingzhou, and took Yanzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 盧循浮海破廣州，獲刺史吳隱之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun came by sea and took Guangzhou, capturing Inspector Wu Yinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun sailed in, seized Guangzhou, and captured Inspector Wu Yinzhi.

sentences.zh: 即以循為廣州刺史，以其同黨徐道覆為始興相。

translations.literal: He then made Xun Inspector of Guangzhou and his partisan Xu Daofu Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He made Xun inspector of Guangzhou and his ally Xu Daofu administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，督交、廣二州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, he was made Commander over Jiao and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year he was made commander over Jiao and Guang.

sentences.zh: 十月，高祖上言曰：「昔天禍皇室，巨狡縱篡，臣等義惟舊隸，豫蒙國恩，仰契信順之符，俯厲人臣之憤，雖社稷之靈，抑亦事由眾濟。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Gaozu submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly heaven sent calamity on the imperial house, and the great villain indulged usurpation; we, your servants, bound by old allegiance, received the state's grace; looking up we matched the talisman of faithful obedience, looking down we roused the fury of ministers; though the spirits of the altars aided us, still the affair was also accomplished by the multitude's strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gaozu memorialized: "When heaven struck the throne, the great traitor usurped power. We old servants of Jin, grateful for grace, rose in loyal fury. The altars helped us, but the people carried the day.

sentences.zh: 其翼獎忠懃之佐，文武畢力之士，敷執在己之謙，用虧國體之大。

translations.literal: To reward the loyal and diligent assistants and the civil and military who gave their full strength, we have held back merit that should be recorded in our own names, to the harm of the great body of the state.
translations.idiomatic: We have been too modest about rewarding the loyal, to the state's hurt.

sentences.zh: 輒申攝眾軍先上，[19]同謀起義，始平京口、廣陵二城，臣及撫軍將軍毅等二百七十二人，并後赴義出都緣道大戰，所餘一千五百六十六人，又輔國將軍長民、故給事中王元德等十人，合一千八百四十八人，乞正封賞。

translations.literal: We therefore report the armies first, [19] fellow conspirators in the righteous rising: first pacifying the two cities Jingkou and Guangling—your servant and Pacifier of the Army Yi and two hundred seventy-two others—and those who joined the cause later, fighting great battles all the way from the capital; the remaining one thousand five hundred sixty-six; also Assistant to the State Changmin and the late Palace Attendant Wang Yuande and ten others: in all one thousand eight hundred forty-eight men, begging regular enfeoffment and reward.
translations.idiomatic: We beg leave to register first the armies of the rising:[19] the two hundred seventy-two who took Jingkou and Guangling, including Yi and myself; the one thousand five hundred sixty-six who fought along the road; Changmin and Yuande and ten more—one thousand eight hundred forty-eight in all—deserving enfeoffment and reward.

sentences.zh: 其西征眾軍，須論集續上。

translations.literal: The western campaign armies must be discussed and reported in a later memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The western armies will be listed in a later memorial.

sentences.zh: 」於是尚書奏封唱義謀主鎮軍將軍裕豫章郡公，食邑萬戶，賜絹三萬匹。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Masters of Writing memorialized enfeoffing the chief righteous plotter, Pacifier of the Army Yu, as Duke of Yuzhang with ten thousand households and thirty thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing recommended enfeoffing Yu, chief of the plot, as Duke of Yuzhang with ten thousand households and thirty thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其餘封賞各有差。

translations.literal: The rest received rewards each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Others were rewarded in due proportion.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍府佐吏，降故太傅謝安府一等。

translations.literal: Staff officers of the Pacifier of the Army were lowered one grade from the former Grand Tutor Xie An's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: His staff were ranked one grade below Xie An's former grand tutorship.

sentences.zh: 十一月，天子重申前令，加高祖侍中，進號車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Son of Heaven repeated the earlier order, promoting Gaozu to Palace Attendant and advancing his title to General of Chariots and Cavalry with the Bountiful Rites Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor again offered him Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and the Three Excellencies rites.

sentences.zh: 固讓。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He refused again.

sentences.zh: 詔遣百僚敦勸。

translations.literal: An edict sent the hundred officials to urge him earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent officials to press him.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，高祖還京師，將詣廷尉，天子先詔獄官不得受，詣闕陳讓，乃見聽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Gaozu returned to the capital and was about to go to the Minister of Justice; the Son of Heaven first ordered the prison officials not to receive him; he went to the palace to decline and was heard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year he returned to the capital. He pretended to submit to the Minister of Justice; the emperor forbade the prison to accept him. He declined at court and was excused.

sentences.zh: 旋于丹徒。

translations.literal: He then returned to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 閏月，府將駱冰謀作亂，將被執，單騎走，追斬之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, a staff officer, Luo Bing, plotted rebellion; about to be seized, he fled alone on horseback; they pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month his officer Luo Bing rebelled, fled on horseback, and was run down and killed.

sentences.zh: 誅冰父永嘉太守球。

translations.literal: Bing's father, Administrator of Yongjia Qiu, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiu, administrator of Yongjia, was executed.

sentences.zh: 球本東陽郡史，孫恩之亂，起義於長山，故見擢用。

translations.literal: Qiu had originally been a clerk of Dongyang commandery; in Sun En's disorder he raised righteousness at Changshan and was therefore promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had been a Dongyang clerk who rose against Sun En at Changshan and was promoted for it.

sentences.zh: 初桓玄之敗，以桓冲忠貞，署其孫胤。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was first defeated, because Huan Chong was loyal and pure, he appointed Chong's grandson Yin.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan's first defeat he had appointed Chong's grandson Yin, honoring Chong's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 至是冰謀以胤為主，與東陽太守殷仲文潛相連結。

translations.literal: By now Bing plotted to make Yin master, secretly linking with Administrator of Dongyang Yin Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Bing meant to set Yin on the throne and conspired with Yin Zhongwen of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 乃誅仲文及仲文二弟。

translations.literal: Zhongwen and his two younger brothers were then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen and his two brothers were executed.

sentences.zh: 凡桓玄餘黨，至是皆誅夷。

translations.literal: All Huan Xuan's remaining partisans were at this time exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The last of Xuan's faction were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 天子遣兼太常葛籍授公策曰：「有扈滔天，夷羿乘釁，亂節干紀，實橈皇極。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Concurrent Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Ge Ji to present the ducal mandate, saying: "Youhu flooded heaven; Yi of Xia seized the opportunity; disordering the seasons and violating the calendar, they truly shook the imperial pole.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Ge Ji with the ducal mandate: "Youhu defied heaven; Yi of Xia seized his chance—they overturned order and shook the throne.

sentences.zh: 賊臣桓玄，怙寵肆逆，乃摧傾華、霍，倒拔嵩、岱，五嶽既夷，六地易所。

translations.literal: The traitor minister Huan Xuan, relying on favor and running wild, overthrew Hua and Huo, uprooted Song and Dai; the five sacred mountains were leveled, the six directions changed their place.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor Xuan, drunk on favor, overthrew the pillars of state as if uprooting sacred mountains.

sentences.zh: 公命世英縱，藏器待時，因心資敬，誓雪國恥，慨憤陵夷，誠發宵寐。

translations.literal: You, hero of the age, hid your talent awaiting the time; with reverence in your heart you swore to wipe away the national shame; indignant at the dynasty's fall, your sincerity rose from night sleep.
translations.idiomatic: You, hero of the age, hid your talent until the hour came, swore to wipe out national shame, and burned with loyalty night and day.

sentences.zh: 既而歲月屢遷，神器已遠，忠孝幽寄，實貫三靈。

translations.literal: Then years passed again and again, the sacred vessel was already far; loyalty and filial piety lodged in the hidden, truly penetrating the three spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed; the throne was lost; your loyalty reached heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 爾乃介石勝機，宣契畢舉，訴蒼天以為正，揮義旅而一驅。

translations.literal: Thereupon you took the firm stone of victory's moment, declared the covenant complete, appealed to azure heaven as your standard, and swept the righteous host in one drive.
translations.idiomatic: You seized the moment, appealed to heaven, and swept the traitors in one charge.

sentences.zh: 奔鋒數百，勢烈激電，百萬不能抗限，制路日直植城。

translations.literal: Charging spears by the hundreds, momentum fierce as lightning, a million could not resist the barrier; the road to the capital stood straight.
translations.idiomatic: Your spears charged like lightning; a million men could not stop you; the road to the capital lay open.

sentences.zh: [20]遂使衝鯨潰流，暴鱗江漢，廟勝遠加，重氛載滌，二儀廓清，三光反照，事遂永代，功高開闢，理微稱謂，義感朕心。

translations.literal: [20] Thus he made the leaping whale break its current, exposed fish in the Jiang and Han; the temple victory reached afar, heavy miasma was washed away; the two regulators were cleared, the three lights shone again; the affair will last ten thousand ages, merit towers over the opening of the age; reason is subtle and hard to name, righteousness moves Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: [20] You broke the rebel flood, cleared the Jiang and Han, restored the realm, and lit the three lights again—merit greater than the founding of an age. Our heart is moved.

sentences.zh: 若夫道為身濟，猶縻厥爵，況乃誠德俱深，勳冠天人者乎。

translations.literal: If the Way aids the person yet still ties up rank, how much more when sincerity and virtue are both deep and merit crowns heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: If even lesser service wins rank, how much more yours, which crowns heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 是用建茲邦國，永祚山河，言念載懷，匪云足報。

translations.literal: Therefore We establish this state, eternal blessing on mountains and rivers; thinking of it fills Our bosom—not words enough for repayment.
translations.idiomatic: We establish this state upon you forever; no reward can repay you.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go forth in reverence!
translations.idiomatic: Go forth in reverence!

sentences.zh: 俾屏余一人，長弼皇晉，流風垂祚，暉烈無窮。

translations.literal: Support Us alone, long aid great Jin, spread your wind and leave your blessing, glory without end.
translations.idiomatic: Support us, uphold Jin, and let your glory endure without end.

sentences.zh: 其降承嘉策，對敭朕命。」

translations.literal: Descend and receive this fine mandate; respond and proclaim Our command."
translations.idiomatic: Receive this mandate and answer Our command."

sentences.zh: 十二月，司徒、錄尚書、揚州刺史王謐薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Minister of Education, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yangzhou Wang Mi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wang Mi died.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，徵公入輔，授侍中、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史、錄尚書，徐兗二州刺史如故。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, the Duke was summoned to assist at court, appointed Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Bountiful Rites Equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Yangzhou, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, with Xu and Yan as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the Duke was called to court as Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, with Three Excellencies rites, Yangzhou, and the recorder's post.

sentences.zh: 表解兗州。

translations.literal: He memorialized to relinquish Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是遣冠軍劉敬宣伐蜀賊譙縱，無功而返。

translations.literal: Earlier Champion Liu Jingxuan had been sent to campaign against the Shu bandit Qiao Zong and returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Jingxuan had failed in an expedition against Qiao Zong in Shu.

sentences.zh: 九月，以敬宣挫退，遜位，不許。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because Jingxuan had been repulsed, he yielded his post; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jingxuan offered to resign after his defeat; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 乃降為中軍將軍，開府如故。

translations.literal: He was then demoted to General of the Central Army, his staff establishment as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to General of the Central Army with his staff unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初偽燕王鮮卑慕容德僭號於青州，德死，兄子超襲位，前後屢為邊患。

translations.literal: Earlier the false Yan king, the Xianbei Murong De, had usurped title in Qingzhou; when De died, his elder brother's son Chao succeeded, repeatedly causing border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei Murong De had set up as Yan king in Qingzhou. When he died, his nephew Chao succeeded and raided the borders repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，大掠淮北，執陽平太守劉千載、濟南太守趙元，驅略千餘家。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, he raided greatly north of the Huai, seizing Administrator of Yangping Liu Qianzai and Administrator of Jinan Zhao Yuan, driving off more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year Chao raided north of the Huai, taking two administrators and more than a thousand families.

sentences.zh: 三月，公抗表北討，以丹陽尹孟昶監中軍留府事。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Duke submitted a memorial for a northern campaign; Administrator of Danyang Meng Chang was made overseer of the central army and left to guard the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Duke memorialized for a northern campaign and left Meng Chang to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 四月，舟師發京都，泝淮入泗。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the fleet left the capital, went up the Huai, and entered the Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the fleet left the capital and sailed up the Huai into the Si.

sentences.zh: 五月，至下邳，留船艦輜重，步軍進琅邪。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, reaching Xiapi, they left ships and baggage; the infantry advanced into Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they reached Xiapi, left the ships, and marched into Langye.

sentences.zh: 所過皆築城留守。

translations.literal: Wherever they passed they built walled posts and left garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: They fortified every place they passed and left garrisons.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑梁父、莒城二戍並奔走。

translations.literal: The Xianbei garrisons at Liangfu and Ju both fled.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons at Liangfu and Ju fled.

sentences.zh: 慕容超聞王師將至，其大將公孫五樓說超：「宜斷據大峴，刈除粟苗，堅壁清野以待之。

translations.literal: When Murong Chao heard the royal army was coming, his great general Gongsun Wulou advised Chao: "You should block and hold the Great Pass, cut the grain shoots, and empty the fields to wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's general Wulou advised: "Hold the Great Pass, burn the crops, and starve them out.

sentences.zh: 彼僑軍無資，求戰不得，旬月之間，折棰以笞之耳。

translations.literal: That foreign army has no supplies; unable to obtain battle, within ten days you can beat them with a stick.
translations.idiomatic: They have no supplies. In ten days you can whip them with a stick."

sentences.zh: 」超不從，曰：「彼遠來疲勞，勢不能久，但當引令過峴，我以鐵騎踐之，不憂不破也。

translations.literal: " Chao did not follow, saying: "They come from afar weary; their momentum cannot last long. Only lead them past the pass; I with iron cavalry will trample them—no worry of not breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: Chao refused: "They are tired from the march. Let them through the pass, then my cavalry will crush them."

sentences.zh: 豈有預芟苗稼，先自䠞弱邪。

translations.literal: How could one beforehand cut the grain shoots and weaken oneself first?
translations.idiomatic: Why burn our own grain first and weaken ourselves?"

sentences.zh: 」初公將行，議者以為賊聞大軍遠出，必不敢戰，若不斷大峴，當堅守廣固，刈粟清野，以絕三軍之資，非唯難以有功，將不能自反。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when the Duke was about to march, counsellors thought that when the bandits heard the great army had gone far out, they would surely not dare fight; if they did not block the Great Pass, they would surely hold Guanggu firmly, cut grain, and empty the fields to cut off the Three Armies' supplies—not only hard to achieve merit, but they might not be able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Before the march, advisers warned that the enemy would hold Guanggu, burn the fields, and starve the army out.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「我揣之熟矣。

translations.literal: The Duke said: "I have thought it through thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke said, "I have weighed it carefully.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑貪，[21]不及遠計，進利剋獲，退惜粟苗。

translations.literal: The Xianbei are greedy, [21] and do not plan for the long term; advancing, they covet quick gain; retreating, they regret the grain shoots.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei are greedy[21] and shortsighted. They want booty now and hate to burn their own fields.

sentences.zh: 謂我孤軍遠入，不能持久，不過進據臨朐，退守廣固。

translations.literal: They think my lone army has entered far and cannot last long—nothing more than advancing to hold Linqu and retreating to guard Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: They think we cannot endure a long campaign—only advance to Linqu or fall back to Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 我一得入峴，則人無退心，驅必死之眾，向懷貳之虜，何憂不剋。

translations.literal: Once we enter the pass, then men will have no heart to retreat; driving troops resolved to die against bandits with divided hearts—why worry of not conquering?
translations.idiomatic: Once we are through the pass, our men will not retreat. We will drive desperate soldiers against wavering foes. How can we fail?"

sentences.zh: 彼不能清野固守，為諸君保之。

translations.literal: They cannot empty the fields and hold firm—I guarantee that for you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: They will not burn the fields. I stake my word on it."

sentences.zh: 」公既入峴，舉手指天曰：「吾事濟矣！」

translations.literal: " Once the Duke had entered the pass, he raised his hand and pointed to heaven, saying: "My affair is assured!"
translations.idiomatic: Inside the pass he pointed to heaven: "Victory is mine!"

sentences.zh: 六月，慕容超遣五樓及廣寧王賀賴盧先據臨朐城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Murong Chao sent Wulou and Prince of Guangning Helai Lu first to hold Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Chao sent Wulou and Helai Lu to hold Linqu.

sentences.zh: 既聞大軍至，留羸老守廣固，乃悉出。

translations.literal: When he heard the great army had arrived, he left the weak and old to guard Guanggu and came out with his full strength.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the army had come, he left the weak in Guanggu and marched out in force.

sentences.zh: 臨朐有巨蔑水，去城四十里。

translations.literal: At Linqu there is the Jumie River, forty li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Forty li from Linqu lay the Jumie River.

sentences.zh: 超告五樓曰：「急往據之，晉軍得水，則難擊也。

translations.literal: Chao told Wulou: "Hurry and seize it; if the Jin army gets water, they will be hard to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Chao told Wulou, "Seize the river. If the Jin army gets water, they are hard to fight."

sentences.zh: 」五樓馳進。

translations.literal: " Wulou galloped forward.
translations.idiomatic: Wulou raced ahead.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍孟龍符領騎居前，奔往爭之，五樓乃退。

translations.literal: General of the Dragon Cavalry Meng Longfu led the cavalry vanguard and ran to contest it; Wulou then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Longfu led the cavalry vanguard to seize it first. Wulou fell back.

sentences.zh: 眾軍步進，有車四千兩，分車為兩翼，方軌徐行，車悉張幔，御者執矟。

translations.literal: The mass army advanced on foot; there were four thousand carts; they divided the carts into two wings, marching in square formation at an easy pace; all carts were draped with curtains, and the drivers held spears.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand carts advanced on foot in two wings, curtains drawn, drivers gripping spears.

sentences.zh: 又以輕騎為遊軍。

translations.literal: They also used light cavalry as roaming troops.
translations.idiomatic: Light cavalry screened the flanks.

sentences.zh: 軍令嚴肅，行伍齊整。

translations.literal: Army orders were strict; ranks and files were orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline was iron; the ranks never broke.

sentences.zh: 未及臨朐數里，賊鐵騎萬餘，前後交至。

translations.literal: Before reaching Linqu by several li, more than ten thousand bandit iron cavalry came from before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: Several li short of Linqu, ten thousand enemy horsemen struck front and rear.

sentences.zh: 公命兗州刺史劉藩、弟并州刺史道憐、諮議參軍劉敬宣、陶延壽、參軍劉懷玉、慎仲道、索邈等，齊力擊之。

translations.literal: The Duke ordered Inspector of Yanzhou Liu Fan, his younger brother Inspector of Bingzhou Daoling, Staff Adviser Liu Jingxuan, Tao Yanshou, Staff Officer Liu Huaiyu, Shen Zhongdao, Suo Miao, and the rest to strike together with full strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke sent Liu Fan, Daoling, Jingxuan, Huaiyu, and others to hit them with everything they had.

sentences.zh: 日向昃，公遣諮議參軍檀韶直趨臨朐。

translations.literal: As the sun tilted west, the Duke sent Staff Adviser Tan Shao straight for Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening he sent Tan Shao straight at Linqu.

sentences.zh: 詔率建威將軍向彌、參軍胡藩馳往，即日陷城，斬其牙旗，悉虜超輜重。

translations.literal: Shao led General Who Establishes Martial Might Xiang Mi and Staff Officer Hu Fan at the gallop; that very day they took the city, cut down its pennant, and captured all Chao's baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Shao with Xiang Mi and Hu Fan took the city that day, struck down its banner, and seized Chao's baggage train.

sentences.zh: 超聞臨朐已拔，引眾走，公親鼓之，賊乃大奔。

translations.literal: When Chao heard Linqu had fallen, he led his masses in flight; the Duke personally beat the drums, and the bandits then fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Chao fled when he heard Linqu had fallen. The Duke beat the drums himself and the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 超遁還廣固。

translations.literal: Chao escaped back to Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Chao ran back to Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 獲超馬、偽輦、玉璽、豹尾等，送于京師。

translations.literal: They captured Chao's horses, false imperial carriage, jade seal, leopard-tail insignia, and the rest, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They took his horses, false imperial carriage, seal, and regalia and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 斬其大將段暉等十餘人，其餘斬獲千計。

translations.literal: They beheaded his great generals Duan Hui and more than ten others; the rest killed or captured numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They killed General Duan Hui and ten others; thousands more were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 明日，大軍進廣固，即屠大城，超退保小城。

translations.literal: The next day, the great army advanced on Guanggu, sacked the outer city at once, and Chao withdrew to hold the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they reached Guanggu, stormed the outer city, and Chao shut himself in the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 於是設長圍守之，圍高三丈，外穿三重塹。

translations.literal: Thereupon they set a long encirclement to besiege it; the rampart was three zhang high, with three ditches dug outside.
translations.idiomatic: They laid a siege with a three-zhang wall and three rings of ditches.

sentences.zh: 停江、淮轉輸，館穀於齊土。

translations.literal: They halted transport from the Jiang and Huai and stored grain in Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: They cut the Jiang-Huai supply line and stored grain in Qi.

sentences.zh: 撫納降附，華戎歡悅，援才授爵，因而任之。

translations.literal: They comforted and accepted those who surrendered; Chinese and barbarians rejoiced; they supported talent and granted ranks, employing men accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Surrenders were welcomed; Chinese and barbarians alike rejoiced; talent was promoted and employed.

sentences.zh: 七月，詔加公北青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, an edict added the Duke as Inspector of northern Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was given northern Qing and Ji as well.

sentences.zh: 超大將垣遵、遵弟苗並率眾歸順。

translations.literal: Chao's great generals Yuan Zun and Zun's younger brother Miao both led their troops in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's generals Yuan Zun and Miao submitted with their troops.

sentences.zh: 公方治攻具，城上人曰：「汝不得張綱，何能為也。

translations.literal: The Duke was just preparing siege engines when men on the wall said: "You cannot draw the net—what can you do?
translations.idiomatic: While siege engines were being built, men on the wall mocked: "Without Zhang Gang, what can you do?"

sentences.zh: 」綱者，超偽尚書郎，其人有巧思。

translations.literal: " Gang was Chao's false Master of Writing gentleman; the man had ingenious skill.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was Chao's engineering officer, a man of ingenious skill.

sentences.zh: 會超遣綱稱藩於姚興，乞師請救。

translations.literal: Presently Chao sent Gang to declare himself a vassal to Yao Xing, begging troops for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent Gang to Yao Xing to beg for aid.

sentences.zh: 興偽許之，而實憚公，不敢遣。

translations.literal: Xing falsely promised, yet in truth feared the Duke and did not dare send.
translations.idiomatic: Xing promised falsely but feared the Duke and sent no one.

sentences.zh: 綱從長安還，泰山太守申宣執送之。

translations.literal: Gang returned from Chang'an; Administrator of Taishan Shen Xuan seized and sent him on.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was returning from Chang'an when Shen Xuan of Taishan seized him.

sentences.zh: 及升綱於樓車，[22]以示城內，城內莫不失色。

translations.literal: When they raised Gang on the tower cart, [22] to show him inside the city, everyone inside lost color.
translations.idiomatic: They raised Gang on a siege tower[22] for the garrison to see. The city went pale.

sentences.zh: 於是使綱大治攻具。

translations.literal: Thereupon they had Gang greatly repair the assault engines.
translations.idiomatic: Then they set Gang to building assault machines.

sentences.zh: 超求救不獲，綱反見虜，轉憂懼。

translations.literal: Chao's plea for rescue was not obtained; Gang in turn was captured; he turned still more anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Rescue never came; Gang was captured; Chao grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 乃請稱藩，求割大峴為界，獻馬千疋。

translations.literal: He then asked to declare himself a vassal, seeking to cede the Great Pass as a border and present a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: He offered to submit, cede the Great Pass, and send a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 不聽，圍之轉急。

translations.literal: They did not listen; the siege grew still tighter.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke refused. The siege tightened.

sentences.zh: 河北居民荷戈負糧至者，日以千數。

translations.literal: North of the He, inhabitants bearing spears and carrying grain arrived by the thousands each day.
translations.idiomatic: Each day thousands from north of the He came with arms and grain to help.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍劉穆之，有經略才具，公以為謀主，動止必諮焉。

translations.literal: Recording Secretary Liu Muzhi had talent for strategy and planning; the Duke made him chief planner, consulting him in every move.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi, a gifted strategist, became his chief adviser; every move passed through him.

sentences.zh: 時姚興遣使告公云：「慕容見與隣好，又以窮告急，今當遣鐵騎十萬，逕據洛陽。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Xing sent a messenger telling the Duke: "Murong Chao is my neighbor in friendship, and again in extremity begs help; now I shall send a hundred thousand iron cavalry straight to seize Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent word: "Chao is my ally and begs help. I will send a hundred thousand horsemen to take Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 晉軍若不退者，便當遣鐵騎長驅而進。

translations.literal: If the Jin army does not withdraw, then I shall send iron cavalry in long drive forward.
translations.idiomatic: If your army does not withdraw, they will ride straight for you."

sentences.zh: 」公呼興使答曰：「語汝姚興，我定燕之後，息甲三年，當平關、洛。

translations.literal: " The Duke called Xing's messenger to answer: "Tell your Yao Xing: after I settle Yan, I shall rest my armor three years, then pacify Guan and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke had the messenger told: "Tell Yao Xing: when Yan falls I shall rest three years, then take Guan and Luo.

sentences.zh: 今能自送，便可速來。

translations.literal: If he can deliver himself now, let him come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: If he wants to save himself, let him come at once."

sentences.zh: 」穆之聞有羌使，馳入，而公發遣已去。

translations.literal: " Muzhi, hearing there was a Qiang envoy, galloped in, but the Duke had already sent the messenger away.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi heard of the envoy and rushed in, but the Duke had already dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 以興所言并答，具語穆之。

translations.literal: He told Muzhi all that Xing had said and the reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke told Muzhi what had been said and answered.

sentences.zh: 穆之尤公曰：「常日事無大小，必賜與謀之。

translations.literal: Muzhi blamed the Duke, saying: "On ordinary days, affairs great and small, you always grant me counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi reproached him: "You always consult me on every matter.

sentences.zh: 此宜善詳之，云何卒爾便答。

translations.literal: This ought to have been weighed carefully—why answer so abruptly?
translations.idiomatic: This deserved careful thought. Why answer in haste?"

sentences.zh: 公所答興言，未能威敵，正足怒彼耳。

translations.literal: The words you answered Xing with cannot awe the enemy; they only anger him.
translations.idiomatic: Your words will not frighten him—only provoke him.

sentences.zh: 若燕未可拔，羌救奄至，不審何以待之？

translations.literal: If Yan cannot yet be taken and Qiang rescue suddenly arrives, I do not know how we shall deal with it?
translations.idiomatic: If Yan holds out and Qiang aid comes, what then?"

sentences.zh: 」公笑曰：「此是兵機，非卿所解，故不語耳。

translations.literal: " The Duke smiled and said: "This is military craft—not something you would understand, so I did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke smiled. "That is military craft—not for you. That is why I did not tell you.

sentences.zh: 夫兵貴神速，彼若審能遣救，必畏我知，寧容先遣信命。

translations.literal: In war, speed is prized; if he could really send rescue, he would fear that we knew and could not allow sending a messenger first.
translations.idiomatic: War prizes speed. If he meant to send troops, he would not announce it first.

sentences.zh: 此是其見我伐燕，內已懷懼，自張之辭耳。」

translations.literal: This is because he sees us attacking Yan and is already afraid within; it is words to puff himself up."
translations.idiomatic: He sees us on Yan and is already afraid. This is bluster."

sentences.zh: 九月，進公太尉、中書監，固讓。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Duke was promoted to Grand Marshal and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was offered Grand Marshal and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing. He refused.

sentences.zh: 偽徐州刺史段宏先奔索虜，十月，自河北歸順。

translations.literal: The false Inspector of Xuzhou Duan Hong had first fled to the northern barbarians; in the tenth month he returned from north of the He in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hong, false inspector of Xuzhou, had fled north; in the tenth month he submitted.

translations.literal: Annotation marker 23.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 23.

sentences.zh: 張綱治攻具成，設諸奇巧，飛樓木幔之屬，莫不畢備。

translations.literal: Zhang Gang finished repairing the assault engines; he set up every sort of ingenious device—flying towers, wooden screens, and the like—nothing lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Gang finished the siege machines—flying towers, screens, every device.

sentences.zh: 城上火石弓矢，無所用之。

translations.literal: Fire stones, bows, and arrows on the wall were of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Stones and arrows on the walls availed nothing.

sentences.zh: 六年二月丁亥，屠廣固。

translations.literal: On dinghai of the second month of the sixth year, Guanggu was sacked.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the second month of the sixth year Guanggu fell.

sentences.zh: 超踰城走，征虜賊曹喬胥獲之，殺其王公以下，[24]納口萬餘，馬二千疋，送超京師，斬于建康市。

translations.literal: Chao fled over the wall; Bandit-Capturing Cao Qiaoxu seized him; the kings, dukes, and below were killed, [24] more than ten thousand captives taken, two thousand horses; Chao was sent to the capital and beheaded in the Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: Chao fled over the wall and was taken by Qiaoxu. The royal clan was slaughtered;[24] ten thousand captives and two thousand horses were taken. Chao was sent to Jiankang and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 公之北伐也，徐道覆仍有窺窬之志，勸盧循乘虛而出，循不從。

translations.literal: When the Duke was on the northern campaign, Xu Daofu still harbored designs of encroachment and urged Lu Xun to strike while the opportunity was void; Xun did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: While the Duke campaigned north, Xu Daofu urged Lu Xun to strike the empty south. Xun refused.

sentences.zh: 道覆乃至番禺說循曰：「本住嶺外，豈以理極於此，正以劉公難與為敵故也。

translations.literal: Daofu then went to Panyu to persuade Xun: "We originally dwelt beyond the ranges—could reason end here? It is only because Lord Liu is hard to match as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu went to Panyu and said: "We came from beyond the ranges. Liu is too strong to fight while he sits on Yan.

sentences.zh: 今方頓兵堅城之下，[25]未有旋日。

translations.literal: Now he is stalled beneath a stout wall, [25] with no day of turning back in sight.
translations.idiomatic: He is stuck before a strong wall[25] with no quick end in sight.

sentences.zh: 以此思歸死士，掩襲何、劉之徒，如反掌耳。

translations.literal: With this, think of the soldiers who long for home—strike He and Liu and the rest—it would be like turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Rally the homesick soldiers and strike He and Liu—it would be easy.

sentences.zh: 不乘此機而保一日之安，若平齊之後，小息甲養眾，不過一二年間，必璽書徵君。

translations.literal: If you do not seize this chance for a day's peace, when Qi is pacified and he rests armor and nourishes the masses, within a year or two an edict with the imperial seal will surely summon you.
translations.idiomatic: Miss this chance and when Qi falls he will rest, then summon you within a year or two.

sentences.zh: 若劉公自率眾至豫章，遣銳師過嶺，雖復將軍神武，恐必不能當也。

translations.literal: If Lord Liu himself leads troops to Yuzhang and sends sharp commanders over the ranges, though you, General, are divine in war, I fear you cannot withstand it.
translations.idiomatic: If Liu comes to Yuzhang and sends veterans over the mountains, even you cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 今日之機，萬不可失。

translations.literal: Today's opportunity must on no account be lost.
translations.idiomatic: This day will not come again.

sentences.zh: 既剋都邑，傾其根本，劉公雖還，無能為也。

translations.literal: Once you take the capital and overturn their root, even if Lord Liu returns, he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Take the capital and cut their root, and Liu can do nothing even if he returns."

sentences.zh: 」循從之，乃率眾過嶺。

translations.literal: " Xun followed him and therefore led his masses over the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Xun agreed and crossed the mountains.

sentences.zh: 是月，寇南康、廬陵、豫章，諸郡守皆委任奔走。

translations.literal: That month they raided Nankang, Luling, and Yuzhang; the commandery administrators all abandoned their posts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That month they ravaged Nankang, Luling, and Yuzhang. Every administrator fled.

sentences.zh: 于時平齊問未至，即馳使徵公。

translations.literal: At that time word that Qi was pacified had not yet arrived; they immediately sent messengers to summon the Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Before news of victory in Qi arrived, messengers raced to recall the Duke.

sentences.zh: 公之初剋齊也，欲停鎮下邳，清盪河、洛，既而被徵使至，即日班師。

translations.literal: When the Duke first took Qi, he had wished to halt and garrison at Xiapi, sweeping He and Luo; then the summons arrived and that very day he turned the army back.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Qi he had meant to hold Xiapi and sweep the north; the summons came and he marched back the same day.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍何無忌與徐道覆戰于豫章，敗績，無忌被害。

translations.literal: Pacifier of the South He Wuji fought Xu Daofu at Yuzhang and was defeated; Wuji was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji fought Daofu at Yuzhang, was beaten, and killed.

sentences.zh: 內外震駭。

translations.literal: Within and without were shaken in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country were terrified.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲奉乘輿北走就公，尋知賊定未至，人情小安。

translations.literal: The court wished to take the imperial carriage north to join the Duke; soon they learned the bandits had not yet arrived and popular feeling calmed a little.
translations.idiomatic: The court thought of fleeing north to the Duke; then learned the rebels had not reached the capital and hearts steadied slightly.

sentences.zh: 公至下邳，以船運輜重，自率精銳步歸。

translations.literal: The Duke reached Xiapi, sent baggage by boat, and himself led picked infantry home by forced march.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiapi he sent baggage by boat and marched home with elite infantry.

sentences.zh: 至山陽，聞無忌被害，則慮京邑失守，乃卷甲兼行，與數十人至淮上，問行旅以朝廷消息。

translations.literal: Reaching Shanyang, he heard Wuji had been killed and feared the capital was lost; he rolled up armor and marched day and night; with several dozen men he reached the Huai and asked travelers for court news.
translations.idiomatic: At Shanyang he heard Wuji was dead and feared the capital had fallen. He forced the march to the Huai and asked travelers for news.

sentences.zh: 人曰：「賊尚未至，劉公若還，便無所憂也。

translations.literal: Someone said: "The bandits have not yet arrived; if Lord Liu returns, there will be nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: They said, "The rebels have not taken the city. If the Duke returns, all is well."

sentences.zh: 」公大喜，單船過江，逕至京口，眾乃大安。

translations.literal: " The Duke was greatly pleased, crossed the river in a single boat, went straight to Jingkou, and the masses were greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoiced, crossed in one boat to Jingkou, and the people took heart.

sentences.zh: 四月癸未，公至京師，解嚴息甲。

translations.literal: On guimao of the fourth month, the Duke reached the capital, lifted the emergency, and rested the armor.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the fourth month he reached the capital, ended the alarm, and rested the troops.

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍劉毅抗表南征，公與毅書曰：「吾往習擊妖賊，曉其變態，新獲姦利，其鋒不可輕。

translations.literal: Pacifier of the Army Liu Yi submitted a memorial for a southern campaign; the Duke wrote Yi: "I am accustomed to striking demonic bandits and know their shifts; newly gained, they are sharp—their point must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi asked to march south. The Duke wrote: "I know these rebels. Fresh from victory, they are dangerous.

sentences.zh: 宜須裝嚴畢，與弟同舉。

translations.literal: You should wait until preparations are complete and march with your younger cousin together.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until you are ready and go with your cousin."

sentences.zh: 」又遣毅從弟藩往止之。

translations.literal: " He also sent Yi's younger cousin Fan to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yi's cousin Fan to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 毅不從，舟師二萬，發自姑孰。

translations.literal: Yi did not follow; a naval force of twenty thousand set out from Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi would not listen. Twenty thousand men sailed from Gushu.

sentences.zh: 循之初下也，使道覆向尋陽，自寇湘中諸郡。

translations.literal: When Xun first came downstream, he sent Daofu toward Xunyang and himself raided the commanderies of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent Daofu to Xunyang and raided Hunan himself.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史道規遣軍至長沙，為循所敗。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Daogui sent troops to Changsha and was defeated by Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui sent troops to Changsha and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 逕至巴陵，將向江陵。

translations.literal: He went straight to Baling and was about to march on Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xun pushed on to Baling and aimed at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 道覆聞毅上，馳使報循曰：「毅兵眾甚盛，成敗事係之於此，宜并力摧之。

translations.literal: Daofu, hearing Yi was coming upstream, galloped with a message to tell Xun: "Yi's soldiers are very numerous; success or failure hangs on this—you should combine strength to crush him.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu heard Yi was coming and urged Xun: "Yi is strong. Everything hangs on beating him now.

sentences.zh: 若此克捷，天下無復事矣。

translations.literal: If this battle is won, there will be nothing more under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Win here and the realm is yours.

sentences.zh: 根本既定，不憂上面不平也。

translations.literal: Once the root is settled, there is no worry that the upper reaches will not be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Secure the base and the upper Yangzi will follow."

sentences.zh: 」循即日發巴陵，與道覆連旗而下。

translations.literal: " Xun set out from Baling that very day and came downstream with Daofu, banners linked.
translations.idiomatic: Xun left Baling the same day and sailed down with linked banners.

sentences.zh: 別有八艚艦九枚，起四層，高十二丈。

translations.literal: Separately there were eight tower ships of nine spans, four stories high, twelve zhang tall.
translations.idiomatic: Eight nine-deck tower ships rose four stories, twelve zhang high.

sentences.zh: 公以南藩覆沒，表送章綬，詔不聽。

translations.literal: Because the southern defense was destroyed, the Duke submitted his seal and cord; an edict did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: After the southern disaster he offered to resign; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 五月，劉毅敗績于桑落洲，棄船步走，餘眾不得去者，皆為賊所擒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Liu Yi was defeated at Sangluo Isle, abandoned his ships and fled on foot; those who could not escape were all captured by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yi was destroyed at Sangluo Isle. Survivors were taken.

sentences.zh: 初循至尋陽，聞公已還，不信也。

translations.literal: When Xun first reached Xunyang, he heard the Duke had already returned and did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang Xun heard the Duke had returned and did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 既破毅，乃審凱入之問，並相視失色。

translations.literal: After defeating Yi, he then verified the news of victory entering and all looked at one another, faces changed.
translations.idiomatic: After beating Yi he learned it was true. Faces fell.

sentences.zh: 循欲退還尋陽，進平江陵，據二州以抗朝廷。

translations.literal: Xun wished to withdraw to Xunyang, advance and pacify Jiangling, and hold the two provinces to resist the court.
translations.idiomatic: Xun wanted to fall back to Xunyang and hold Jing with Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 道覆謂宜乘勝徑進，固爭之。

translations.literal: Daofu said they ought to press the victory and advance straight on; he argued firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu insisted they press the attack.

sentences.zh: 疑議多日，乃見從。

translations.literal: After many days of dispute, he was at last obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: After days of argument Xun agreed.

sentences.zh: 毅敗問至，內外洶擾。

translations.literal: When news of Yi's defeat arrived, within and without were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: News of Yi's defeat threw the court into panic.

sentences.zh: 于時北師始還，多創痍疾病。

translations.literal: At that time the northern army had just returned, many wounded and ill.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army had just returned, wounded and sick.

sentences.zh: 京師戰士，不盈數千。

translations.literal: Capital fighting men numbered no more than a few thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had only a few thousand fit fighters.

sentences.zh: 賊既破江、豫二鎮，戰士十餘萬，舟車百里不絕。

translations.literal: The bandits, having broken the Jiang and Yu garrisons, had a hundred thousand or more warriors; ships and carts stretched a hundred li without break.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had a hundred thousand men and a hundred li of ships.

sentences.zh: 奔敗還者，並聲其雄盛。

translations.literal: Those who fled back all proclaimed their might.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives magnified their strength.

sentences.zh: 孟昶、諸葛長民懼寇漸逼，欲擁天子過江，公不聽，昶固請不止。

translations.literal: Meng Chang and Zhuge Changmin, fearing the bandits drew near, wished to take the Son of Heaven across the river; the Duke did not listen; Chang repeatedly begged without end.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and Changmin wanted to move the emperor across the river. The Duke refused.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「今重鎮外傾，強寇內逼，人情危駭，莫有固志。

translations.literal: The Duke said: "Now the great garrisons abroad have fallen, a strong bandit presses within, hearts are terrified, and none has a firm will.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The borders have fallen and a great enemy is at the gates. Panic would destroy us.

sentences.zh: 若一旦遷動，便自瓦解土崩，江北亦豈可得至！

translations.literal: If we move in a single day, we shall dissolve and collapse like earth; how could we even reach the north of the Jiang!
translations.idiomatic: Flee now and we collapse. We would never reach the north bank.

sentences.zh: 設令得至，不過延日月耳。

translations.literal: Even if we could reach it, it would only prolong the months.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we did, it would only buy days.

sentences.zh: 今兵士雖少，自足以一戰。

translations.literal: Today our soldiers, though few, are enough for one battle.
translations.idiomatic: We are few but enough for one fight.

sentences.zh: 若其克濟，則臣主同休；

translations.literal: If we succeed, lord and ministers share rest;
translations.idiomatic: Win, and lord and minister survive together.

sentences.zh: 苟厄運必至，我當以死衞社稷，橫尸廟門，遂其由來以身許國之志，不能遠竄於草間求活也。

translations.literal: if ill fortune must come, I shall die guarding the altars, corpses before the temple gate, fulfilling the resolve from of old to give my person to the state—I cannot flee far into the grass to seek life.
translations.idiomatic: If fate turns against us, I die at the temple gates as I always vowed. I will not skulk in the grass for life.

sentences.zh: 我計決矣，卿勿復言！

translations.literal: My plan is fixed; speak no more!
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made. Say no more."

sentences.zh: 」昶恐其不濟，乃為表曰：「臣裕北討，眾並不同，唯臣贊裕行計，致使強賊乘間，社稷危逼，臣之罪也。

translations.literal: " Chang, fearing he would not succeed, then made a memorial saying: "Your servant Yu on the northern campaign—all disagreed; only your servant approved Yu's plan, causing a strong bandit to seize the interval; the altars are in peril—it is your servant's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, fearing defeat, memorialized: "I alone urged the northern campaign. The realm is in peril through my fault.

sentences.zh: 今謹引分以謝天下。

translations.literal: Now I respectfully yield my portion to apologize to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to atone with my life."

sentences.zh: 」封表畢，乃仰藥而死。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was sealed, he took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the memorial and took poison.

sentences.zh: 於是大開賞募，投身赴義者，一同登京城之科。

translations.literal: Thereupon great rewards were opened for recruitment; those who threw in their persons for righteousness received the same rank as scaling the capital wall.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were posted; volunteers won the same honors as storming the wall.

sentences.zh: 發居民治石頭城，建牙戒嚴。

translations.literal: The populace was mobilized to repair Shitou, banners were raised, and the army was put on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Citizens repaired Shitou; the army was called to arms.

sentences.zh: 時議者謂宜分兵守諸津要。

translations.literal: At the time counsellors said troops should be divided to guard the strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers wanted to split forces among the passes.

sentences.zh: 公以為：「賊眾我寡，若分兵屯，則人測虛實。

translations.literal: The Duke thought: "The bandits are many, we few; if we divide troops to garrison, men will measure our emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke said, "They are many, we few. Split forces and they see our weakness.

sentences.zh: 且一處失利，則沮三軍之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, if one place is lost, it will damp the spirit of the Three Armies.
translations.idiomatic: One defeat breaks every heart.

sentences.zh: 今聚眾石頭，隨宜應赴，既令賊無以測多少，又於眾力不分。

translations.literal: Now gather the masses at Shitou and respond as fit—this both keeps the bandits from measuring how many we are and does not divide the strength of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Mass at Shitou and strike where needed. They cannot count us, and we stay strong.

sentences.zh: 若徒旅轉集，徐更論之耳。

translations.literal: If foot and horse gradually assemble, we may discuss it again later.
translations.idiomatic: When more troops gather, we can adjust."

sentences.zh: 」移屯石頭，乃柵淮斷查浦。

translations.literal: " He moved camp to Shitou and then palisaded the Huai and cut off Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Shitou and fortified the Huai line at Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 既而羣賊大至，公策之曰：「賊若於新亭直進，其鋒不可當，宜且回避，勝負之事，未可量也。

translations.literal: When the bandit masses arrived in great numbers, the Duke calculated: "If the bandits advance straight from Xinting, their point cannot be withstood; we should for the moment avoid them—the matter of victory or defeat cannot yet be measured.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came he judged: "If they land at Xinting we cannot stop them. If they moor west of the river, we take them."

sentences.zh: 若回泊西岸，此成擒耳。」

translations.literal: If they turn and moor on the west bank, they are prey to capture."
translations.idiomatic: If they moor west of the river, they are ours."

sentences.zh: 道覆欲自新亭、白石焚舟而上。

translations.literal: Daofu wished to go from Xinting and Baishi, burning boats as they advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu wanted to land at Xinting and Baishi and burn their boats.

sentences.zh: 循多疑少決，每欲以萬全為慮，謂道覆曰：「大軍未至，孟昶便望風自裁，大勢言之，自當計日潰亂。

translations.literal: Xun was suspicious and slow to decide; he always wanted to plan for complete safety and said to Daofu: "The great army has not yet arrived, yet Meng Chang surrendered at the rumor of the wind—the great trend says they will collapse within days.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was timid. He told Daofu: "The capital will collapse on its own. Why fight today and waste men?"

sentences.zh: 今決勝負於一朝，既非必定之道，且殺傷士卒，不如按兵待之。

translations.literal: To settle victory or defeat in a single morning is not a sure path, and wounding soldiers—better hold the army and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Better wait than gamble a morning battle."

sentences.zh: 」公于時登石頭城以望循軍，初見引向新亭，公顧左右失色。

translations.literal: " The Duke at the time mounted Shitou to watch Xun's army; when he first saw them heading for Xinting, he looked to those beside him, faces changed.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke watched from Shitou. When the fleet turned toward Xinting, his officers paled.

sentences.zh: 既而回泊蔡洲。

translations.literal: Presently they turned and moored at Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Then they swung to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 道覆猶欲上，循禁之。

translations.literal: Daofu still wished to land; Xun forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu still wanted to land. Xun forbade it.

sentences.zh: 自是眾軍轉集，修治越城，築查浦、藥園、廷尉三壘，皆守以實眾。

translations.literal: From then on the armies gradually assembled; they repaired Yuecheng and built the three forts Zhapu, Yaoyuan, and Tingwei, all held with solid troops.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements gathered. They fortified Yuecheng, Zhapu, Yaoyuan, and Tingwei.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍劉敬宣屯北郊，輔國將軍孟懷玉屯丹陽郡西，建武將軍王仲德屯越城，廣武將軍劉懷默屯建陽門外。

translations.literal: Champion General Liu Jingxuan encamped at the northern suburb; Assistant to the State Meng Huaiyu encamped west of Danyang commandery; General Who Establishes Martial Might Wang Zhongde encamped at Yuecheng; General of Broad Martial Liu Huaimo encamped outside Jianyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan held the north suburb, Huaiyu west of Danyang, Zhongde Yuecheng, Huaimo Jianyang Gate.

sentences.zh: [26]使寧朔將軍索邈領鮮卑具裝虎班突騎千餘匹，皆被練五色，自淮北至于新亭。

translations.literal: [26] He sent General Who Pacifies the North Suo Miao to lead more than a thousand fully armored Xianbei tiger-spot lancers, all clad in white silk of five colors, from north of the He to Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: [26] He sent Suo Miao with a thousand armored Xianbei lancers in five-colored white silk from the north to Xinting.

sentences.zh: 賊並聚觀，咸畏憚之；

translations.literal: The bandits all gathered to watch and were awed and in fear;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels watched in awe;

sentences.zh: 然猶冀京邑及三吳有應之者。

translations.literal: yet they still hoped that the capital region and the three Wu would have responders.
translations.idiomatic: yet still hoped the capital and Wu would rise for them.

sentences.zh: 遣十餘艦來拔石頭柵，公命神弩射之，發輒摧陷，循乃止不復攻柵。

translations.literal: They sent more than ten ships to pull up the Shitou palisade; the Duke ordered divine crossbows to shoot them; every shot smashed and sank them; Xun then stopped and no longer attacked the palisade.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to pull up the Shitou stakes. Crossbows smashed their ships. Xun gave up.

sentences.zh: 設伏兵於南岸，使羸老悉乘舟艦向白石。

translations.literal: He set ambush troops on the south bank and had the weak and old all board boats toward Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: He hid troops on the south bank and sent weak men in boats toward Baishi.

sentences.zh: 公憂其從白石步上，乃率劉毅、諸葛長民北出拒之，留參軍徐赤特戍南岸，命堅守勿動。

translations.literal: The Duke feared they would land from Baishi on foot; he therefore led Liu Yi and Zhuge Changmin north to meet them, leaving Staff Officer Xu Chite to garrison the south bank with orders to hold firm and not move.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a landing at Baishi, he took Yi and Changmin north, leaving Xu Chite on the south bank with orders to hold.

sentences.zh: 公既去，賊焚查浦步上，赤特軍戰敗，死沒有百餘人。

translations.literal: Once the Duke had gone, the bandits burned Zhapu and came up on foot; Chite's army was defeated in battle, and more than a hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: Once he left, the rebels burned Zhapu and crossed. Chite was beaten; a hundred died.

sentences.zh: 赤特棄餘眾，單舸濟淮。

translations.literal: Chite abandoned the remainder, crossed the Huai in a single boat.
translations.idiomatic: Chite fled alone across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 賊遂率數萬屯丹陽郡。

translations.literal: The bandits then led tens of thousands to encamp at Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels camped tens of thousands at Danyang.

sentences.zh: 公率諸軍馳歸。

translations.literal: The Duke led the armies in galloping return.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke raced his army back.

sentences.zh: 眾憂賊過，咸謂公當徑還拒戰。

translations.literal: The masses feared the bandits had passed by and all said the Duke ought to return straight and resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Men thought the rebels had passed and urged him to turn and fight at once.

sentences.zh: 公先分軍還石頭，眾莫之曉。

translations.literal: The Duke first sent part of the army back to Shitou; none understood why.
translations.idiomatic: He sent part of the force back to Shitou first. No one understood.

sentences.zh: 解甲息士，洗浴飲食之，乃出列陳於南塘。

translations.literal: He removed armor and rested the soldiers, had them bathe, eat, and drink, then came out and drew up ranks at Nantang.
translations.idiomatic: He let the men rest, wash, and eat, then formed them on the south embankment.

sentences.zh: 以赤特違處分，斬之。

translations.literal: Because Chite had violated orders, he beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Chite for disobeying orders.

sentences.zh: 命參軍褚叔度、朱齡石率勁勇千餘人過淮。

translations.literal: He ordered Staff Officers Chu Shudu and Zhu Lingshi to lead more than a thousand stalwarts across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chu Shudu and Zhu Lingshi with a thousand picked men across the Huai.

sentences.zh: [27]羣賊數千，皆長刀矛鋋，精甲曜日，奮躍爭進。

translations.literal: [27] The bandit masses numbered several thousand, all with long sabers, spears, and ge hooks; fine armor gleamed in the sun as they leaped forward competing to advance.
translations.idiomatic: [27] Several thousand rebels came with long blades and bright armor, charging in the sun.

sentences.zh: 齡石所領多鮮卑，善步矟，並結陳以待之。

translations.literal: Those under Lingshi were mostly Xianbei, skilled at infantry spears; they all formed ranks to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi's men were mostly Xianbei spearmen in tight formation.

sentences.zh: 賊短兵弗能抗，死傷者數百人，乃退走。

translations.literal: The bandits with short weapons could not resist; several hundred were killed or wounded, and they then retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Short weapons failed them. Hundreds fell. They fled.

sentences.zh: 會日莫，眾亦歸。

translations.literal: As the day ended, the masses also returned.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk both sides withdrew.

sentences.zh: 劉毅之敗，豫州主簿袁興國反叛，據歷陽以應賊。

translations.literal: After Liu Yi's defeat, Chief Clerk of Yuzhou Yuan Xingguo rebelled and held Liyang in response to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi's defeat, Yuan Xingguo of Yuzhou rebelled and held Liyang for the rebels.

sentences.zh: 琅邪內史魏順之遣將謝寶討斬之。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Langye Wei Shunzhi sent General Xie Bao to campaign and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shunzhi sent Xie Bao, who killed him.

sentences.zh: 興國司馬襲寶，順之不救而退，公怒斬之。

translations.literal: Xingguo's marshal attacked Bao; Shunzhi did not rescue him and withdrew—the Duke in anger beheaded Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingguo's officer struck Bao; Shunzhi would not help and retreated. The Duke had Shunzhi executed.

sentences.zh: 順之，詠之之弟也。

translations.literal: Shunzhi was the younger brother of Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi was Yongzhi's brother.

sentences.zh: 於是功臣震懾，莫敢不用命。

translations.literal: Thereupon the meritorious ministers were awed and none dared not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers were terrified into obedience.

sentences.zh: 六月，更授公太尉、中書監，加黃鉞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Duke was again appointed Grand Marshal and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, with the yellow battle-axe added.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was again offered Grand Marshal, supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and the yellow axe.

sentences.zh: 受黃鉞，餘固辭。

translations.literal: He accepted the yellow battle-axe; the rest he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He took the axe but refused the rest.

sentences.zh: 以司馬庾悅為建威將軍、江州刺史，自東陽出豫章。

translations.literal: Staff Officer Yu Yue was made General Who Establishes Martial Might and Inspector of Jiangzhou, advancing from Dongyang toward Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue was sent as inspector of Jiangzhou from Dongyang toward Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 七月庚申，羣賊自蔡洲南走，還屯尋陽。

translations.literal: On gengshen of the seventh month, the bandit masses went south from Caizhou and returned to encamp at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the seventh month the rebels left Caizhou and camped again at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 遣輔國將軍王仲德、廣川太守劉鍾、河間太守蒯恩追之。

translations.literal: He sent Assistant to the State Wang Zhongde, Administrator of Guangchuan Liu Zhong, and Administrator of Hejian Kuai En in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhongde, Liu Zhong, and Kuai En in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 公還東府，大治水軍，皆大艦重樓，高者十餘丈。

translations.literal: The Duke returned to the eastern headquarters and greatly built the navy; all were large ships with layered towers, the tallest more than ten zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Back at headquarters he built a great fleet of tower ships ten zhang high.

sentences.zh: 盧循遣其大將荀林寇江陵，[28]桓謙先於江陵奔羌，又自羌入蜀，偽主譙縱以為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Lu Xun sent his great general Xun Lin to raid Jiangling; [28] Huan Qian had earlier fled from Jiangling to the Qiang, and again from the Qiang entered Shu; the false ruler Qiao Zong made him Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent Xun Lin against Jiangling.[28] Huan Qian had fled to the Qiang and then to Shu, where Qiao Zong made him inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 謙及譙道福率軍二萬，出寇江陵，適與林會，相去百餘里。

translations.literal: Qian and Qiao Daofu led twenty thousand troops out to raid Jiangling and happened to meet Lin, a hundred li or more apart.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and Qiao Daofu marched twenty thousand men on Jiangling and met Lin a hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史道規斬謙于枝江，破林於江津，追至竹町斬之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Daogui beheaded Qian at Zhijiang and broke Lin at Jiangjin, pursuing to Zhuting and beheading him.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui killed Qian at Zhijiang, beat Lin at Jiangjin, and hunted him down at Zhuting.

sentences.zh: 初循之走也，公知其必寇江陵，登遣淮陵內史索邈領馬軍步道援荊州。

translations.literal: When Xun first fled, the Duke knew he would surely raid Jiangling and had sent Interior Minister of Huailing Suo Miao to lead horse troops by foot road to aid Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Xun would threaten Jiangling, he had sent Suo Miao overland to aid Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又遣建威將軍孫季高率眾三千，自海道襲番禺。

translations.literal: He also sent General Who Establishes Martial Might Sun Jigao to lead three thousand men by sea route to strike Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Sun Jigao with three thousand men by sea against Panyu.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史庾悅至五畝嶠，賊遣千餘人據斷嶠道，悅前驅鄱陽太守虞丘進攻破之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiangzhou Yu Yue reached Wumu Pass; the bandits sent more than a thousand men to hold and cut the pass road; Yue's vanguard, Administrator of Poyang Yuqiu Jin, broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue reached Wumu Pass; rebels blocked the road; Jin broke through.

sentences.zh: 公治兵大辦。

translations.literal: The Duke's preparation of troops was greatly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Preparations for the campaign were complete.

sentences.zh: 十月，率兗州刺史劉藩、寧朔將軍檀韶等舟師南伐。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he led Inspector of Yanzhou Liu Fan, General Who Pacifies the North Tan Shao, and the rest in a naval southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he sailed south with Fan, Shao, and the fleet.

sentences.zh: 以後將軍劉毅監太尉留守府，後事皆委焉。

translations.literal: Rear General Liu Yi was made overseer of the Grand Marshal's rear headquarters; all rear affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi was left to guard the capital with full authority.

sentences.zh: 是月，徐道覆率眾三萬寇江陵。

translations.literal: That month, Xu Daofu led thirty thousand men to raid Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: That month Daofu struck Jiangling with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史道規又大破之，斬首萬餘級，道覆走還盆口。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Daogui again routed them completely, beheading more than ten thousand; Daofu fled back to Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui routed him again, took ten thousand heads, and drove Daofu back to Penkou.

sentences.zh: 初公之遣索邈也，邈在道為賊所斷，道覆敗後方達。

translations.literal: When the Duke had sent Suo Miao, Miao on the road was cut off by bandits and only reached after Daofu's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Miao had been cut off on the road and arrived only after Daofu's defeat.

sentences.zh: 自循東下，江陵斷絕京邑之問，傳者皆云已沒。

translations.literal: From the time Xun came downstream, Jiangling was cut off from the capital's communications; messengers all said it had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: While Xun was downstream, word said Jiangling had fallen.

sentences.zh: 及邈至，方知循走。

translations.literal: When Miao arrived, they then knew Xun had fled.
translations.idiomatic: Miao's arrival brought the truth: Xun had fled.

sentences.zh: 循初自蔡洲南走，留其親黨范崇民五千人，高艦百餘，戍南陵。

translations.literal: When Xun first fled south from Caizhou, he left his intimate partisan Fan Chongmin with five thousand men and more than a hundred tall ships to garrison Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing south, Xun left Fan Chongmin with five thousand men and a hundred ships at Nanling.

sentences.zh: 王仲德等聞大軍且至，乃進攻之。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhongde and the rest heard the great army was about to arrive, they advanced to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde attacked when the main fleet approached.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大破崇民軍，焚其舟艦，收其散卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, they routed Chongmin's army completely, burned his ships, and gathered his scattered troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they destroyed Chongmin, burned his fleet, and gathered survivors.

sentences.zh: 循廣州守兵，不以海道為防。

translations.literal: Xun's Guangzhou garrison did not guard against the sea route.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou never expected an attack by sea.

sentences.zh: 是月，建威將軍孫季高乘海奄至，而城池峻整，兵猶數千。

translations.literal: That month, General Who Establishes Martial Might Sun Jigao came suddenly by sea; the walls were high and firm, and fighting men still numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jigao appeared by sea. The city was strong, with thousands of defenders.

sentences.zh: 季高焚賊舟艦，悉力而上，四面攻之，即日屠其城。

translations.literal: Jigao burned the bandit ships, exerted all strength to go up, attacked on four sides, and sacked the city that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao burned the fleet, stormed on every side, and took the city the same day.

sentences.zh: 循父以輕舟奔始興。

translations.literal: Xun's father fled in a light boat to Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's father escaped by boat to Shixing.

sentences.zh: 季高撫其舊民，戮其親黨，勒兵謹守。

translations.literal: Jigao comforted the old inhabitants, executed the intimate partisans, and restrained the troops in strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao pacified the people, killed Xun's kin, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 初公之遣季高也，眾咸以海道艱遠，必至為難；

translations.literal: When the Duke first sent Jigao, the masses all thought the sea route arduous and far and that it would surely be difficult;
translations.idiomatic: When Jigao was sent, all said the sea route was too risky.

sentences.zh: 且分撤見力，二三非要。

translations.literal: moreover, dividing and scattering visible strength was not the essential plan two or three times over.
translations.idiomatic: Splitting forces seemed unwise.

sentences.zh: 公不從。

translations.literal: The Duke did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 敕季高曰：「大軍十二月之交，必破妖虜。

translations.literal: He charged Jigao: "When the great army meets at the turn of the twelfth month, it will surely break the demonic bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He told Jigao: "By mid-twelfth month I will break the rebels.

sentences.zh: 卿今時當至廣州，傾其巢窟，令賊奔走之日，無所歸投。

translations.literal: You now must reach Guangzhou in time, overturn their nest and cave, and when the bandits flee in flight, leave them nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Reach Guangzhou on time and destroy their base so they have nowhere to run."

sentences.zh: 」季高受命而行，如期剋捷。

translations.literal: " Jigao received the charge and marched; on schedule he achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao obeyed and took the city on schedule.

sentences.zh: 循方治兵旅舟艦，設諸攻備。

translations.literal: Xun was just repairing troops and boats and setting up every sort of assault preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was still fitting out ships and siege gear.

sentences.zh: 公欲御以長算，乃屯軍雷池。

translations.literal: The Duke wished to meet them with long calculation and therefore encamped the army at Leichi.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke camped at Leichi to wear them down.

sentences.zh: 賊揚聲不攻雷池，當乘流逕下。

translations.literal: The bandits proclaimed they would not attack Leichi but would ride the current straight downstream.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels claimed they would sail past Leichi downstream.

sentences.zh: 公知其欲戰，且慮賊戰敗，或於京江入海，遣王仲德以水艦二百於吉陽下斷之。

translations.literal: The Duke knew they wished to fight and, fearing that if defeated in battle they might enter the sea at Jingjiang, sent Wang Zhongde with two hundred war boats below Jiyang to cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: He knew they meant to fight. Fearing a escape to sea, he posted Zhongde at Jiyang with two hundred ships.

sentences.zh: 十二月，循、道覆率眾數萬，方艦而下，前後相抗，莫見舳艫之際。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xun and Daofu led tens of thousands of men, square ships downstream; before and after they opposed one another, and one could not see where the sterns met.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xun and Daofu came downriver with tens of thousands in a forest of masts.

sentences.zh: 公悉出輕利鬭艦，躬提幡鼓，命眾軍齊力擊之。

translations.literal: The Duke sent out all the light, nimble fighting ships, himself grasping banner and drum, ordering the armies to strike together with united strength.
translations.idiomatic: He sent light warships, took the drum himself, and ordered a mass attack.

sentences.zh: 又上步騎於西岸。

translations.literal: He also set infantry and cavalry on the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry and cavalry lined the west bank.

sentences.zh: 右軍參軍庾樂生乘艦不進，斬而徇之。

translations.literal: Right Army Staff Officer Yu Lesheng rode a ship and did not advance; he was beheaded and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lesheng hung back; he was beheaded as an example.

sentences.zh: 於是眾軍並踊騰爭先。

translations.literal: Thereupon the armies all leaped and strove to be first.
translations.idiomatic: The army surged forward.

sentences.zh: 軍中多萬鈞神弩，所至莫不摧陷。

translations.literal: In the army were many ten-thousand-jun divine crossbows; wherever they reached, nothing failed to be smashed.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-thousand-jun crossbows smashed everything they touched.

sentences.zh: 公中流蹙之，因風水之勢，賊艦悉泊西岸。

translations.literal: The Duke was wounded by a stray arrow in the flow; by the momentum of wind and water, the bandit ships all moored on the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow struck the Duke. Wind and current drove the enemy ships to the west bank.

sentences.zh: 岸上軍先備火具，[29]乃投火焚之，煙爓張天，賊眾大敗，追奔至夜乃歸。

translations.literal: The army on the shore had prepared fire equipment beforehand, [29] and then cast fire and burned them; smoke and flames filled the sky; the bandit masses were greatly defeated; pursuit ran until night before they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shore troops had fire ready[29] and burned the fleet. Smoke filled the sky. The enemy was destroyed. Pursuit lasted until night.

sentences.zh: 循等還尋陽。

translations.literal: Xun and the rest returned to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled back to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 初分遣步軍，莫不疑怪，及燒賊艦，眾乃悅服。

translations.literal: When infantry had first been sent out separately, all were puzzled; when the bandit ships were burned, the masses were then pleased and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: The separate infantry march had puzzled men; burning the fleet won their trust.

sentences.zh: 召王仲德，請還為前驅。

translations.literal: He summoned Wang Zhongde and asked him to return as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Zhongde as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 留輔國將軍孟懷玉守雷池。

translations.literal: Assistant to the State Meng Huaiyu was left to guard Leichi.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyu was left at Leichi.

sentences.zh: 循聞大軍上，欲走向豫章，乃悉力柵斷左里。
