translations.literal: When Xun heard the great army was coming upstream, he wished to flee toward Yuzhang and therefore used all strength to palisade and block Zuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the army was coming, Xun fortified Zuoli on the road to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 大軍至左里，將戰，公所執麾竿折，折幡沈水，眾並怪懼。

translations.literal: When the great army reached Zuoli and was about to fight, the banner staff the Duke held snapped; the broken pennant sank in the water, and all were startled and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At Zuoli his banner pole snapped and the pennant sank. Men were alarmed.

sentences.zh: 公歡笑曰：「往年覆舟之戰，幡竿亦折，今者復然，賊必破矣。

translations.literal: The Duke laughed and said: "In the year of the capsized boat battle, the banner staff also snapped; now it is so again—the bandits will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: He laughed: "The pole snapped at the river battle too. The rebels will break."

sentences.zh: 」即攻柵而進。

translations.literal: " He at once attacked the palisade and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked the palisade at once.

sentences.zh: 遁兵雖殊死戰，弗能禁。

translations.literal: The fleeing soldiers fought to the death and could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fought desperately but could not hold.

sentences.zh: 諸軍乘勝奔之，循單舸走。

translations.literal: The armies, riding victory, chased them; Xun fled in a single boat.
translations.idiomatic: The army chased. Xun escaped in one boat.

sentences.zh: 所殺及投水死，凡萬餘人。

translations.literal: Those killed and those who died casting themselves into the water numbered more than ten thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand were killed or drowned.

sentences.zh: 納其降附，宥其逼略。

translations.literal: He accepted those who surrendered and pardoned those who had been coerced.
translations.idiomatic: Surrenders were accepted; the coerced were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 遣劉藩、孟懷玉輕軍追之。

translations.literal: He sent Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu with light troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Huaiyu pursued with light troops.

sentences.zh: 循收散卒，尚有數千人，逕還廣州。

translations.literal: Xun gathered scattered troops and still had several thousand men, going straight back to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xun regrouped a few thousand and ran for Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 道覆還保始興。

translations.literal: Daofu returned to hold Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu held Shixing.

sentences.zh: 公旋自左里。

translations.literal: The Duke returned from Zuoli himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke withdrew from Zuoli.

sentences.zh: 天子遣侍中、黃門勞師于行所。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent a Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate to comfort the army at the place of march.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to congratulate the army on campaign.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 彭城縣綏輿里人 各本並奪去「輿」字。

translations.literal: The people of Suirenyu li in Pengcheng—each edition omits the character 輿.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding Suirenyu li in Pengcheng: all editions drop the character yu (輿).

sentences.zh: 御覽一二八引徐爰宋書作「彭城綏輿里人」。

translations.literal: Imperial Readings 128 cites Xu Ai's Song Shu as "a man of Suirenyu li, Pengcheng."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Readings 128 quotes Xu Ai's Song Shu: "of Suirenyu li, Pengcheng."

sentences.zh: 符瑞志中附會祥瑞，云：元嘉二十一年，「甘露降彭城綏輿里」。

translations.literal: The Records of Portents, in attaching auspicious omens, says: "In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, sweet dew fell on Suirenyu li in Pengcheng."
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Portents records that in Yuanjia 21 sweet dew fell on Suirenyu li in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 南史亦有「輿」字。

translations.literal: The Southern History also has the character 輿.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern History also has yu (輿).

sentences.zh: 今據補。

translations.literal: Now supplemented according to this evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The character is restored here on that authority.

sentences.zh: 恩以彭排自載 「彭排」各本並作「鼓排」。

translations.literal: En used a pengpai to carry himself—"pengpai" in all editions reads "drum-pai" (鼓排).
translations.idiomatic: En boarded a pengpai raft—the text reads "drum-pai" (鼓排) in all editions.

sentences.zh: 御覽三五七引晉安帝紀作「彭排」，今據改。

translations.literal: Imperial Readings 357 cites the Annals of Emperor An of Jin as "pengpai"; now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Readings 357 has pengpai in the Jin Annals; the text is emended to match.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡傳亦有「見軍人擔彭排戰具」語，釋名：「彭排，彭，旁也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e's biography also has the phrase "seeing soldiers carrying pengpai battle gear."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e's biography also mentions soldiers carrying pengpai equipment.

sentences.zh: 在旁排敵禦攻也。」

translations.literal: Explaining Names: "Pengpai—peng means beside; it is set at the side to repel the enemy and ward off attack."
translations.idiomatic: Explaining Names: "Pengpai—peng means at the side; it is placed alongside to fend off attack."

sentences.zh: 領水軍追討至鬱洲 「討」各本作「罰」，據元龜一八四改。

translations.literal: Leading the navy in pursuit to Yuzhou—"pursue" (討) in all editions reads "punish" (罰); changed according to Yuance 184.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the navy in pursuit to Yuzhou: editions read "punish" (罰) instead of "pursue" (討); emended per Yuance 184.

sentences.zh: 通鑑亦作「討孫恩於鬱洲」。

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian also reads "campaign against Sun En at Yuzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian likewise has "campaign against Sun En at Yuzhou."

sentences.zh: 高祖與牢之甥東海何無忌並固諫不從 「諫」各本並作「請」，據南史改。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Laozhi's nephew He Wuji of Donghai together remonstrated firmly and were not obeyed—"remonstrate" (諫) in all editions reads "request" (請); changed according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and He Wuji remonstrated together: editions read "request" (請) for "remonstrate" (諫); emended per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 憑之從子韶韶弟祗隆道濟 各本不疊「韶」字，又「道濟」上有「與叔」二字。

translations.literal: Pingzhi's cousin Shao, Shao's younger brothers Zhi, Zhi, Long, and Daoji—all editions do not repeat the character Shao, and above Daoji there are the two characters "and uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Shao, Zhi, Long, and Daoji: editions omit the repeated "Shao," and insert "and uncle" before Daoji.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「祗、隆、道濟並韶弟，依文義當疊『韶』字。

translations.literal: Sun Fen's Discussion of the Song Shu says: "Zhi, Long, and Daoji are all Shao's younger brothers; according to the sense the character Shao should be repeated."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen notes that Zhi, Long, and Daoji are Shao's brothers and the name Shao should be repeated.

sentences.zh: 」今據孫說補。

translations.literal: Now the character Shao is supplemented according to Sun's statement.
translations.idiomatic: The repeated "Shao" is restored on Sun Fen's authority.

sentences.zh: 張熷讀史舉正云：「韶、祗、道濟並兄弟，此云『與叔』，誤。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng's Corrections in Reading History says: "Shao, Zhi, and Daoji are brothers; to say 'and uncle' here is an error."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng: "Shao, Zhi, and Daoji are brothers; 'and uncle' is wrong."

sentences.zh: 」今據張說刪。

translations.literal: Now deleted according to Zhang's statement.
translations.idiomatic: Deleted on Zhang Sheng's authority.

sentences.zh: 東莞臧熹 「熹」各本並作「喜」，據臧質傳改。

translations.literal: Zang Xi of Dongguan—"Xi" in all editions reads "Xi" (喜); changed according to Zang Zhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi of Dongguan: editions read xi (喜) for xi (熹); emended per Zang Zhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 既而嫌邁不執安穆使得逃去 「嫌」各本並作「廉」，據通鑑晉安帝元興三年改。

translations.literal: Then resenting that Mai did not seize Anmu and let him escape—"resent" (嫌) in all editions reads "Lian" (廉); changed according to Zizhi Tongjian, third year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting that Mai let Anmu escape: editions read "Lian" (廉) for "resent" (嫌); emended per Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 玄又遣武騎將軍庾禕之 晉書桓玄傳作「武衞將軍庾頤之」。

translations.literal: Xuan also sent General of Martial Cavalry Yu Yizhi—the Jin Shu biography of Huan Xuan reads "Defender-in-Chief Yu Yizhi."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yizhi, General of Martial Cavalry: Jin Shu has Defender-in-Chief Yu Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 立留臺官 三朝本、毛本作「立留臺官」。

translations.literal: Establishing the rear-court officials—Sanchao and Mao editions read "establish rear-court officials."
translations.idiomatic: Establishing rear-court officials: Sanchao and Mao editions have this reading.

sentences.zh: 北監本、殿本、局本作「立留臺總百官」。

translations.literal: Northern, Imperial, and Palace editions read "establish rear-court to oversee the hundred offices."
translations.idiomatic: Other editions read "establish the rear court to oversee all offices."

sentences.zh: 通鑑作「立留臺百官」。

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian reads "establish the rear-court and the hundred offices."
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian has "establish the rear court and the hundred offices."

sentences.zh: 按時晉安帝尚在尋陽，故建康稱留臺。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor An of Jin was still at Xunyang, so Jiankang was called the rear court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An was still at Xunyang, so the capital was termed the rear court.

sentences.zh: 據下文眾欲推劉裕領揚州，裕固辭，則此時劉裕必無總百官之事。

translations.literal: According to the passage below where the multitude wished to urge Liu Yu to take Yangzhou and Yu firmly declined, at this time Liu Yu certainly had no business overseeing the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Yu later refused Yangzhou, he could not yet have overseen all offices.

sentences.zh: 以此知作「總百官」者，誤。

translations.literal: From this one knows that those who read "oversee the hundred offices" are in error.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore "oversee the hundred offices" is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 尚書王嘏率百官奉迎乘輿 「王嘏」各本並作「王假」，據南史及通鑑改。

translations.literal: Minister of the Interior Wang Dan led the hundred officials to welcome the imperial carriage—"Wang Dan" in all editions reads "Wang Jia"; changed according to the Southern History and Zizhi Tongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan welcomed the emperor: editions read Wang Jia; emended per Southern History and Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 晉書王導傳：「嗣孫嘏，歷領軍、尚書。」

translations.literal: Jin Shu, biography of Wang Dao: "His descendant Dan succeeded him, successively holding Defender-in-Chief and Minister of the Interior."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shu, Wang Dao: his descendant Dan held Defender-in-Chief and Minister of the Interior.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍徐州刺史 御覽一二八引徐爰宋書、魏書島夷劉裕傳、建康實錄並作「鎮軍將軍」。

translations.literal: Defender-in-Chief and Inspector of Xuzhou—Imperial Readings 128 citing Xu Ai's Song Shu, Wei Shu account of the island barbarian Liu Yu, and Jiankang shilu all read "General Who Pacifies the Army."
translations.idiomatic: Defender-in-Chief and inspector of Xuzhou: other sources read General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「領軍與都督刺史異職，晉書及宋本紀同卷後進位侍中詔皆作『鎮軍將軍』，則都督刺史加號也。

translations.literal: Sun Fen's Discussion of the Song Shu says: "Defender-in-Chief and Commander-in-Chief of the provinces are different offices; the Jin Shu and the basic annals of this volume, in the later promotion to Palace Attendant, both read General Who Pacifies the Army—then Commander-in-Chief and Inspector are added titles.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen: Defender-in-Chief and provincial commander differ; later promotions read General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 當從之。

translations.literal: One should follow that.
translations.idiomatic: That reading should be preferred.

sentences.zh: 然高祖時蓋兼領軍，南史書領軍在徐州刺史下。」

translations.literal: Yet in Gaozu's time he probably also held Defender-in-Chief; the Southern History places Defender-in-Chief below Inspector of Xuzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu likely held Defender-in-Chief as well; the Southern History lists it under inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 由是王謐等諸人時失民望 「時失民望」，北監本、殿本作「時眾民望」。

translations.literal: Thereby Wang Mi and the rest at the time lost the people's regard—"lost the people's regard" in Northern Imperial and Palace editions reads "the multitude's regard."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi and others had lost popular regard: some editions read "the multitude's regard."

sentences.zh: 三朝本、毛本、局本作「時失民望」。

translations.literal: Sanchao, Mao, and Palace editions read "lost the people's regard."
translations.idiomatic: Sanchao, Mao, and Palace editions have "lost the people's regard."

sentences.zh: 李慈銘宋書札記云：「當作時失人望」。

translations.literal: Li Ciming's Notes on the Song Shu says: "It should read lost the people's regard (人望)."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming: read "lost popular regard" (人望).

sentences.zh: 今從三朝本、毛本、局本。

translations.literal: Now following Sanchao, Mao, and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: The Sanchao/Mao/Palace reading is followed.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳卞承之 「卞承之」各本並作「丁承之」。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Household Bian Chengzhi—"Bian Chengzhi" in all editions reads "Ding Chengzhi"; changed according to the Jin Shu biography of Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Chengzhi: editions read Ding; emended per Jin Shu.

sentences.zh: 據晉書桓玄傳改。

translations.literal: According to Zizhi Tongjian, in the third year of Yixi when Yin Zhongwen was executed, Bian Chengzhi was also executed—probably the same man.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian executes Bian Chengzhi with Yin Zhongwen in Yixi 3—likely the same man.

sentences.zh: 按通鑑晉安帝義熙三年殺殷仲文時，並誅卞承之，蓋即其人。

translations.literal: According to Zizhi Tongjian, in the third year of Yixi when Yin Zhongwen was executed, Bian Chengzhi was also executed—probably the same man.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian executes Bian Chengzhi with Yin Zhongwen in Yixi 3—likely the same man.

sentences.zh: 桓玄兄子歆 「兄子歆」各本並作「兒子韶」。

translations.literal: Elder brother's son Xin of Huan Xuan—"elder brother's son Xin" in all editions reads "son Shao"; changed according to Zizhi Tongjian, third year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's nephew Xin: editions read "son Shao"; emended per Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 據通鑑晉安帝元興三年改。

translations.literal: Changed according to Zizhi Tongjian, third year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Emended per Zizhi Tongjian, Yuanxing 3 under Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 道規破玄大將郭銓等于桑落洲 「郭銓」各本作「鄭鈐」，舊本臨川王道規傳

translations.literal: Daogui defeated Xuan's great general Guo Qian and the rest at Sangluo Isle—"Guo Qian" in all editions reads "Zheng Ling"; the old edition of the biography of Linchuan Prince Daogui
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qian at Sangluo Isle: editions read Zheng Ling; the biography of Prince Daogui of Linchuan

sentences.zh: (新本已改正)

translations.literal: (the new edition has already corrected this)
translations.idiomatic: (already corrected in the new edition)

sentences.zh: 及御覽一二八引徐爰宋書作「郭鈐」，本書劉懷肅傳及晉書桓玄傳、通鑑作「郭銓」。

translations.literal: and Imperial Readings 128 citing Xu Ai's Song Shu read "Guo Ling"; this book's biography of Liu Huaisu and the Jin Shu biography of Huan Xuan and Zizhi Tongjian read "Guo Qian."
translations.idiomatic: other sources read Guo Ling or Guo Qian; Guo Qian is correct.

sentences.zh: 按作「郭銓」是，今改正。

translations.literal: According to this, to read Guo Qian is correct; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qian is adopted.

sentences.zh: 眾軍下擊大破之 「眾軍」各本並作「眾驚」，據元龜一八四改。

translations.literal: The armies struck from below and routed them completely—"the armies" in all editions reads "the masses were alarmed"; changed according to Yuance 184.
translations.idiomatic: "The armies" was written "the masses were alarmed" in editions; emended per Yuance 184.

sentences.zh: 璩弟子脩之時為玄屯騎校尉 「脩之」各本並譌「循之」，據南史及通鑑改。

translations.literal: Jin's younger cousin Xiuzhi was then Xuan's Colonel of Valiant Cavalry—"Xiuzhi" in all editions is corrupt as "Xunzhi"; changed according to the Southern History and Zizhi Tongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi miswritten Xunzhi in editions; emended per Southern History and Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 玄從子振逃於華容之涌中 「涌中」各本作「浦中」，據南史及晉書桓彝傳曾孫振附傳改。

translations.literal: Xuan's nephew Zhen fled into the marshes of Huarong—"in the marshes" in all editions reads "in the ford"; changed according to the Southern History and the attached biography of Zhen, great-grandson of Huan Yi, in the Jin Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Fled into the Huarong marshes: editions read "ford"; emended per Southern History and Jin Shu.

sentences.zh: 按杜預左傳莊十八年注：「涌水在南郡華容縣。

translations.literal: According to Du Yu's commentary on Zuo Zhuan, eighteenth year of Duke Zhuang: "The Yong River is in Huarong county, Nan commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu: the Yong River is in Huarong, Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 」水經江水注：「江水又東，涌水注之。

translations.literal: Commentary on the Water Classic, Jiang waters: "The Jiang again flows east, and the Yong River flows into it.
translations.idiomatic: Water Classic: the Yong enters the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 水自夏水南通於江，謂之涌口。」

translations.literal: The water from summer connects south to the river, called the Yong mouth."
translations.idiomatic: Its mouth is called Yongkou."

sentences.zh: 輒申攝眾軍先上 「申」字三朝本空白，各本作「輒攝眾軍」，不空白。

translations.literal: Thereupon reported the armies first—"thereupon" in the Sanchao edition is blank; all editions read "thereupon gathering the armies" without blank space.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon reported the armies first: Sanchao leaves a gap; other editions lack shen (申).

sentences.zh: 今據元龜一八四補。

translations.literal: Now supplemented according to Yuance 184.
translations.idiomatic: Shen (申) is restored per Yuance 184.

sentences.zh: 制路日直植城 句有譌。

translations.literal: The road to the capital stood straight to the city—the sentence is corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase about the road to the capital is corrupt.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑貪 南史作「鮮卑性貪」。

translations.literal: The Xianbei are greedy—the Southern History reads "the Xianbei nature is greedy."
translations.idiomatic: Southern History: "the Xianbei nature is greedy."

sentences.zh: 通鑑作「鮮卑貪婪」。

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian reads "the Xianbei are greedy and grasping."
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian: "greedy and grasping."

sentences.zh: 乃升綱於樓車 「樓車」各本並作「樓上」，據通鑑改。

translations.literal: Then raised Gang on the tower cart—"tower cart" in all editions reads "on the tower"; changed according to Zizhi Tongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Raised on a tower cart: editions read "on the tower"; emended per Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 十月自河北歸順 各本並無「自」字。

translations.literal: In the tenth month returned in submission from north of the He—all editions lack the character "from."
translations.idiomatic: Returned from north of the He: editions omit "from."

sentences.zh: 通鑑晉義熙五年作「段宏自魏奔於裕」。

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, sixth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, reads "Duan Hong fled from Wei to Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian: "Duan Hong fled from Wei to Yu."

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「河北上當有自字」。

translations.literal: Sun Fen's Discussion of the Song Shu says: "Above Hebei there should be the character from."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen: zi (自) should be added before Hebei.

sentences.zh: 按孫說是，今補。

translations.literal: According to Sun, this is correct; now supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Zi (自) is added on his authority.

sentences.zh: 殺其王公以下 「王公」各本作「亡命」，據南史、元龜一八四、通鑑晉安帝義熙六年改。

translations.literal: Killed the kings, dukes, and below—"kings and dukes" in all editions reads "fugitives"; changed according to the Southern History, Yuance 184, and Zizhi Tongjian, sixth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Killed the royal clan: editions read "fugitives"; emended per Southern History and Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 今方頓兵堅城之下 「頓」各本並作「領」，據建康實錄、通鑑晉安帝義熙六年改。

translations.literal: Now stalled beneath a stout wall—"stalled" in all editions reads "led"; changed according to Jiankang shilu and Zizhi Tongjian, sixth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Stalled beneath a stout wall: editions read "led"; emended per Jiankang shilu and Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 廣武將軍劉懷默屯建陽門外 「劉懷默」各本並作「劉默」，據晉書安帝紀、建康實錄補。

translations.literal: General of Broad Martial Liu Huaimo encamped outside Jianyang Gate—"Liu Huaimo" in all editions reads "Liu Mo"; supplemented according to the Jin Shu Annals of Emperor An, Jiankang shilu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaimo at Jianyang Gate: editions read Liu Mo; restored per Jin Shu and Jiankang shilu.

sentences.zh: 懷默見劉懷慎傳。

translations.literal: Huaimo is seen in the biography of Liu Huaishen.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimo appears in Liu Huaishen's biography.

sentences.zh: 命參軍褚叔度朱齡石率勁勇千餘人過淮 「褚叔度」各本並譌「諸葛叔度」。

translations.literal: Ordered Staff Officers Chu Shudu and Zhu Lingshi to lead stalwarts across the Huai—"Chu Shudu" in all editions is corrupt as "Zhuge Shudu."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Shudu miswritten Zhuge Shudu in editions.

sentences.zh: 據通典兵典改。

translations.literal: Changed according to the Tongdian, Military Institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Emended per Tongdian, Military Institutions.

sentences.zh: 又見本書褚叔度傳，時為中軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Also seen in this book's biography of Chu Shudu; at the time he was Middle Army Staff Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: See Chu Shudu's biography; he was then middle-army staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 盧循遣其大將荀林寇江陵 臨川王道規傳作「荀林」。

translations.literal: Lu Xun sent his great general Xun Lin to raid Jiangling—the biography of Linchuan Prince Daogui reads "Xun Lin."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Lin: Daogui's biography agrees.

sentences.zh: 晉書姚興載記及通鑑作「苟林」。

translations.literal: The Jin Shu account of Yao Xing and Zizhi Tongjian read "Gou Lin."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shu and Zizhi Tongjian read Gou Lin.

sentences.zh: 今本書一律作「荀林」。

translations.literal: This book uniformly reads "Xun Lin."
translations.idiomatic: This book consistently uses Xun Lin.

sentences.zh: 岸上軍先備火具 各本並奪「岸」字，據南史、通典兵典、通鑑晉安帝義熙六年補。

translations.literal: The army on the shore had prepared fire equipment beforehand—all editions omit the character "shore"; supplemented according to the Southern History, Tongdian Military Institutions, and Zizhi Tongjian, sixth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Shore troops had fire ready: editions omit "shore"; restored per Southern History, Tongdian, and Zizhi Tongjian.
